**Tests**: Mandatory. This feature's spec and constitution (11.4.224, 11.4.27, 11.4.169) require test-first work with the RED run observed before implementation and every PASS backed by machine-produced evidence. Tasks marked `[TDD]` name the RED condition.

**Organization (deviation from the template, stated)**: the template groups phases by user story. This feature is an audit-and-remediation programme whose work packages cut across all seven user stories, and docs/21 fixes the execution order by dependency (P0 foundation to P7 closure). The phases below therefore follow docs/21 P0-P7; every task carries its `[USn]` tag so a story-ordered view is a filter, not a re-plan. Phase P0 plays the template's Setup role, P1-P2 its Foundational role (no audit or fix work starts before P1 exit and the P2 baselines), and P3-P7 carry the user-story work (US1 register, US2 audit, US3 fixes and evidence, US4 documentation, US5 per-application coverage, US6 dependencies, US7 commit and push hygiene).

## Format: `- [ ] Tnnn [P] [USn] [markers] Description with exact path`

- **[P]**: parallel-safe (different files, no unfinished dependency)
- **[USn]**: user story from spec.md (US1..US7)
- **[TDD]**: RED-GREEN-REFACTOR, RED observed on the broken artifact before implementation
- **[REVIEW]**: independent Opus-xhigh review gate (11.4.142/11.4.209), reviewer stream separate from producer (11.4.240), started by the conductor through the Workflow tool's `agent()` path with model and effort set, its verdict accompanied by the provenance record that `scripts/review/check_review_provenance.sh` validates (T094a, T094d; plan KC-P1)
- **[SUBAGENT]**: can be delegated to a subagent
- **BLOCKED-ON ODG-nn**: waits for the owner decision (doc21 section 8, research.md OD ids); the safe default is stated where research.md defines one
- Paths marked `(new)` do not exist yet and were chosen by the plan; the reviewer confirms them. In every phase, a path that a task creates and that does not exist at the plan commit is a deliverable of the task that names it, whether or not it carries the mark (the phase-group blocks restate this)

## Constraints that bind every task

Rootless Podman containers only; every build of every component in any language (source compile, image production, codegen, render) runs in a rootless container on the remote build host, dispatched event-driven with one authenticated completion record consumed exactly once and no polling or blocking wait, its artifacts brought back and verified by sha256 and digest before use (11.4.173, 11.4.108, 11.4.232; owner decision C1 recorded by T012a: no local-build option and no local-build deviation; a build with no reachable qualified host is `blocked-unavailable`, never run locally); no CI/CD (11.4.156); no force-push, ff-only to all upstreams, a diverged branch integrated by a merge commit and never by a rebase or reset (11.4.113, T042); all work on main branches (FR-024); no credential value in any file (11.4.10); a real service or device is required for every non-unit check, and when it is absent the result is `blocked-unavailable`, never a pass (spec clarification A2); every fix leaves a RED, three GREEN, a caught mutation and an independent GO review (docs/04, docs/06).

## Shared abbreviations (apply to every phase)

| Abbreviation | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `$FEAT` = `$SPEC` | `specs/001-full-project-audit-remediation` |
| `$EV` | `$FEAT/evidence` (ledger.jsonl of `ev/1` entries, class `evidence-ledger` with its own size bound (check class row, T040b), anchors, blobs, verdicts; docs/06 section 11); fixed subfolders `reviews/` (every `[REVIEW]` verdict), `hc/` (human checkpoints), `coverage_baseline/<app>/` (plus one file directly in it, `coverage_baseline/coverage-tools-existence.json`, T200a) and `coverage_targets/<app>/` (never a folder named `coverage/`, which `.gitignore:139` ignores at any depth); every other `$EV/<name>/` folder or `$EV/<name>.json` file is owned by the task that first writes it, which names it |
| `$CPA_RUN` | the run directory of one CPA run, `.audit/commit-push/<run_id>/` (ignored by the T004 `/.audit/` rule, never tmpfs, so a crashed run leaves its stage files for the anti-mess sweep; named `$EVID` until rev 8, renamed because docs/08 §6.1 uses `$EVID` for `$EV/web`); `<run_id>` is the UTC start time to the second, the process id and a random suffix (for example `20261003T120000Z-41234-9f3ac2e1`), so two runs never share one; every output of the run lives there and nowhere else: `report.json` (written last, holding the sha256 of every other file of the directory), `summary.txt`, the stage transcripts, the S7 verifier JSON `verify.json`, the deferral rows, the `/out` directories of the run's container checks, its disk-headroom records, the §9.2 backups of a merge integration under `backup/` and of a `--commit-before-integrate` run under `backup/s1a/`, the result of its S1 settle call under `settle/` (T042), the merge record `merge.json` written before `git merge` starts, with the run's process id and process start time (so a merge left in progress is attributed to its run, as interrupted only once that process is gone and as the lock holder while it lives, T040, T042) and the conflicting files of a refused merge under `conflicts/` (T042); the resolver of a refused merge writes its resolution under the ignored `.audit/merge-resolution/<run_id>/` of the refused run, which CPA only reads (T042); the only files outside it that CPA writes are the ignored `.audit/pending_pins.tsv` (T042a) and the lock and registry records under the ignored `.audit/longops/`, written through `scripts/longops/acquire.sh` and `release.sh` (T089), and the only directories it moves out of the tracked tree are the checkouts of deleted nested gitlinks that its S1 settle call of the T435a helper retires to the ignored `.audit/removed/<run_id>/` (T042) |
| CPA run record | what a task cites for a CPA run, since nothing of the run lands in the tracked tree: after the run has exited, the caller captures `$CPA_RUN/report.json` and `$CPA_RUN/verify.json` with `tools/evidence/evrec -- cat <file>` (an `ev/1` entry whose stdout blob `$EV/blobs/<sha256>` is the file byte for byte, so its sha256 is the file's), or, before the recorder exists (T050), copies them into the task's `$EV/<wp>/` folder with their lines in `$EV/<wp>/SHA256SUMS`; the entry, blob or copy is an ordinary member of the caller's next declared change set, committed by a later CPA run; git itself records every run that committed (its `CPA-Run:` trailer) |
| clean tracked tree | what every clean-tree gate measures (the T161 freeze, the `dirty` field of the T225 and T300 run manifests, T085, T178, T302 and the WP-73 final checks): `scripts/repo/verify_repos.sh --no-remote` (T032) reports `summary.dirty` equal to `summary.dirty_excepted`, each repository judged by `git status --porcelain --ignore-submodules=all` with untracked files counted and ignored paths such as `.audit/` outside it, excepted rows coming only from the reviewed `scripts/repo/exceptions.tsv` (T032); pointer drift is reported beside it, a drift equal to a row of `.audit/pending_pins.tsv` named as a pending pin move (T042a); because CPA writes nothing into the tracked tree, the tree is clean right after a CPA run that exits 0 or 14; the gate cites, by its report sha256, the CPA run record of the run that made the measured HEAD (its run id read from the `CPA-Run:` trailer of that commit, so a later run that committed nothing cannot change the citation; this table governs the rule, which docs/02 §12.1 (rev 7), docs/06 §11 rule 4, docs/16 rule 5, docs/12 and docs/21 IC-42 and IC-47 (rev 11) state as well), or records `report_sha256: null` with a reason when HEAD is not a CPA commit or that report is absent on this host; a test asserts this condition, never a raw `git status --porcelain`, which prints ` M <path>` for a submodule whose content is dirty or whose HEAD moved even when the tracked tree is clean (plan owner's rule (f), rev 9) |

| `$WI` / `$DB` | the constitution `workable-items` binary and `docs/workable_items.db` (ODG-11 default, OD-11) |

`check_pins.sh`, T105; the QA bank validator, T210); measured, in the change set that registers the check, over the check's scope in the main repository and in every own-organisation repository at every depth, each path keyed from the main-repository root as the secret baseline is (T040a; plan owner's rule (W), rev 10), so a `--repo` run (the only way a commit is made inside a submodule, T042 `path_in_submodule`) scores that repository against its own rows and never meets its existing violations as new keys (T042a); S3 fails when a count of a declared file rises, when a new key appears in a declared file, or when a declared file's count falls below its row while the change set leaves the row unchanged, so a baseline may only shrink and follows every reduction (§11.4.135); under `--repo` a declared file whose count falls below its row is reported `baseline_lowering_owed` (key, row count, new count, run id), never 10, because a `--repo` change set cannot declare the main-repository baseline file, and the main-mode change set that moves that repository's gitlink (G-PIN: T442, T581) lowers the row: the files a gitlink move declared in a change set brings into the main tree (those that differ between the old and the new recorded commit, nested gitlinks followed) are held to the lowering rule as declared files of that change set, so the move without the lowering gives 10 (plan owner's decision after the round-11 reviews, T040, T042a), and every row below its count at the new pin is lowered there, whether a `baseline_lowering_owed` report names it or another actor's commit in the moved range made the reduction, which S3 also reports as `baseline_drift` (lowered) (plan owner's decision after the round-12 reviews); the revision-header check applies to every declared Markdown file of a class that applies it, whatever its row, so a file that a change set edits gains the header and its row is lowered in the same change set (T040); a key outside the declared files that an S1 integration brought in (another clone's commits, the gitlinks they move included), and a new or raised key in the files a declared gitlink move brings in from another actor's commits, never this change set's own work, is reported `baseline_drift`, never a refusal of the run that reports it, and registered at the next window as a finding through the T092 path, whose owed action is a fix of the file, never a row added or a count raised: a key above its row or absent from the baseline closes when a change set removes the violation (until then a change set that declares that file gives 10, because there its key is new or above its row), and a count that the drift lowered closes when a change set lowers the row to it (T040). Bootstrap rule: a baseline file is created only in the change set that registers its check (a new `validate_checks.tsv` row, or an existing row switched from mode `deferred` to `ratchet`, which counts as registering it, T040), with a header naming the commit it was measured on and the review verdict that holds it (round-26 review I-3): the baseline file and its registration, an exact `G-GATE` path, are committed as a held commit whose awaited verdict, not yet GO (a hold on a verdict that already holds GO is refused with 20 `verdict_already_go`), is exactly the verdict the header names, the run exiting 14 and S6 pushing nothing before that GO; GO only in the approved form, a run whose owner-approved manifest (T042) holds the registration and admits it unheld (round-25 review I1; rev 32; plan owner's rule (X), rev 10); after that, no row is added and no count raised |

no class exempts a file from the secret fold, except that a fixture root of `scripts/repo/fixture_roots.txt` is exempt from the checks its row lists (T040a, T235); a change to these tables counts only with its review, and while it is held on that review only the paths held on the same verdict are judged with the declared tables, every other path with the HEAD tables, an unheld path being refused only when it fails under the HEAD tables a check that the held tables would pass (20 `table_admits_unheld_path`), never for a stricter difference, and a `--repo` run judging with the tables below every unreleased held main-repository table commit (T040b) |

| `TIC <app> <lane> -- cmd` | top layer: the WP-12 lane dispatcher `scripts/test-in-container.sh <app> <lane> -- cmd` (T121); takes an application and a lane (not an image id), looks the row up in `scripts/containers/lanes.tsv` and dispatches through the matching `run_*.sh` wrapper (the `tooling` rows to `run_testutil.sh`, IMG-TESTUTIL; the `docs` rows to `run_docs.sh`, IMG-DOCS; the `qa` rows, added by T212, to `run_qa.sh`; the app keys `catalogizer-api-client`, `catalogizer-desktop`, `installer-wizard`, `build-scripts` and one key per TypeScript submodule, and the lane `rust`, added by T200a with the wrappers `run_rust.sh` (IMG-RUST, remote) and `run_kcov.sh` (IMG-KCOV, local), so every TIC call with them depends on T200a), which in turn calls `RUNP`-style `podman run`. The three names are layered, not one mechanism: before WP-12 only `RUNP` exists |
| `CPA` | `scripts/commit-push-all.sh` (WP-04, docs/21 IC-16), always started through the host entry point `cpa-host` (rev 32, owner decision of 2026-10-05; `$CPA_HOST_ENTRY`, default `$HOME/.local/bin/cpa-host`, installed and trusted only by the owner, T042, T046a), so `CPA <args>` in this list means `cpa-host <args>`, which executes only the copies of CPA's files that the owner approved, the tracked file started directly exiting 20 `not_via_host_entry`; conductor rule (scoped to the owner's real `$CPA_HOST_STATE` and `$CPA_HOST_ENTRY` and the run directories of real checkouts; a test drives its own test-state `cpa-host` on the T039 harness, CENTRAL C3): every caller, conductor or stream, starts CPA only as `cpa-host`, and no agent installs or edits `cpa-host` or its state directory, invokes `cpa-host --owner-trust`, or creates or writes a run directory's `released/`, which only `cpa-host` writes, the owner-only acts being confirmed at a terminal (§11.4.66): every commit and push from its recorded adoption (T047, after the T046 G-GATE GO) goes through it, in commit windows (P0-P1 conventions), on `main`, pushing fast-forward only, never `--force`, and integrating a diverged repository only by a merge commit it makes itself, never by a rebase or reset (plan owner's rule (Y), rev 10, T042); the declared change set is the explicit path list `--paths-from FILE`, where a path with a review verdict in its second column is committed as a held commit, pushed only once that verdict, read from the main-repository HEAD whatever repository holds the commit, is GO and names the commit's run (review verdict row; `--awaits-review <verdict>` holds every path of the run); a main-mode run commits only in the main repository, a declared path below a gitlink, held or not, being refused before any commit (20 `path_in_submodule`, remediation `CPA --repo <path>`, then the G-PIN pointer move; T042); `--local-only` commits without pushing, `--repo <path>` commits inside one owned repository (T042a), `--commit-before-integrate` commits the declared change set before it integrates a moved remote, the sanctioned remediation of `ff_blocked_by_local_changes` (T042); CPA never writes into the tracked tree and never commits its own outputs, which stay in `$CPA_RUN`; each commit it creates carries the trailer `CPA-Run: <run_id>` and, in its message body, the run's deferral flags (`Deferred-Gates:` with `SKIP_LONG`, `SWEEP_ABSENT` or `LOCAL_ONLY`, `SKIP_LONG` recorded at S0, so a CPA merge commit carries it too), on a held commit the review it waits for (`Awaits-Review: <verdict path>`, a path from the main-repository root), and the commits above that repository's adoption anchor (T047) that are not CPA commits and that a live remote tip held at S1, brought in from another clone or track (a CPA commit by the one T042 predicate, round-25 review B1: its `CPA-Run: <id>` run's record `commits.tsv` in this clone lists its sha, or a committed GO lists its repository path, sha and run id in `covers_runs`; a copied or forged trailer proves nothing) (`Foreign-Commit: <sha>`; a commit that is not a CPA commit and that no remote holds, in any owned repository the run may push, is refused and never named or pushed, T040, T041) (T042); after an S1 fast-forward or merge it settles the gitlinks that move changed through the T435a helper `record_pending_pin.sh --settle-nested`, inside its own lock hold (T042, T042a); one reviewed table decides which paths need which review gate, `scripts/repo/path_gates.tsv` (round-22 review: a path class mapped to its required gate: class `gitlink`, every staged mode-160000 entry, to `G-PIN` with its sha matched against `accepted_pins`; class `cpa_code`, every file `scripts/repo/cpa_code.txt` names, and the exact paths `scripts/repo/cpa_code.txt`, `scripts/repo/path_gates.tsv`, `scripts/repo/host_entry/cpa-host`, `scripts/repo/host_entry/INSTALL.md`, `scripts/repo/validate_checks.tsv`, `scripts/repo/commit_push.conf` and `$FEAT/contracts/review-verdict.schema.json` (round-25 review M2; every verdict check reads the schema from its approved copy, rev 32), to `G-GATE`, `build/containers/images.lock.yaml` among the files `cpa_code.txt` names; class `release_seam`, every file that the union of the HEAD, declared and approved `scripts/release/release_seam_files.txt` names (seeded empty at adoption; a path the HEAD or declared list names that the declared tree lacks gives 20 `release_seam_list_stale` at S2, the approved copy only widening the gated set, CENTRAL C1), and the exact paths `scripts/release/release_seam_files.txt` and `scripts/qa/guard_registry.tsv`, to `G-GATE` (round-26 review M-1); the admission tables of T040b, `scripts/repo/fixture_roots.txt` among them, have no row and follow only T040b's held-table rule, round-23 review M3, an incoming S1 change to one of them by a commit that is not a CPA commit reviewed for `G-GATE` being integrated only by a held merge whose first parent's tables decide S2 and S3 until its merge-review GO is released (T040, T040b, round-25 review M2); T042): at S2 a declared path of a gated class must be held, on any verdict path, which need not exist yet, or admitted by a GO that already names its content (a gitlink under `--accepted-pins`, a file of a `G-GATE` row whose sha256 is its approved manifest entry, rev 32), else 20 `path_gate_unheld`, one verdict holding paths of as many classes as its gate list covers (round-23 decision); at S5 a declared GO must hold in its gate list (`gate`, a gate id or a list of them, contracts revision 16; exact ids, a missing gate counting as a mismatch) the gate of every gated path in the union of the paths that the commits it covers change, each against its first parent (round-26 review I-2: never a path that only a lower held commit awaiting another verdict changes), whose net object, from the released commit to the newest commit that GO releases, changes and is not exempt, and, for `G-PIN`, an `accepted_pins` entry equal to each such net sha (20 `verdict_gate_mismatch`, `verdict_pins_incomplete`), so a NO-GO revert whose net change is none needs no entry; at S6 of a main-mode run the net gitlink change against each pushed remote's tip must be accepted by the GO of its last mover in the pushed range, the newest held commit whose resulting sha at that path equals the net sha (round-24 review M6) (20 `outgoing_gitlink_not_accepted`); at S5 and S6 a path whose new object a reachable remote tip of `main` already records at that path is exempt, a G-GATE path only when that blob's sha256 is its approved manifest entry (T042, rev 32), so a held merge that brings in a published pin, or CPA code the owner approved, is released by a plain GO, while a foreign change to CPA code, which S1 integrates only by a held merge, needs a merge-review GO whose gate list includes `G-GATE` (round-23 review I4); CPA and its helpers execute only from the owner-approved copies that `cpa-host` materialises into `$CPA_RUN/released/` (the released copy, T042), and a bootstrap or a defective release is remedied only by the owner approving a reviewed `G-GATE` GO (T046a) |
| review verdict | the verdict file of a `[REVIEW]` task, `$EV/reviews/<gate-or-wp>[-<item>][-r<n>].json`, in the contract `review-verdict/1` (`$FEAT/contracts/review-verdict.schema.json`; CPA's merge-review files `$EV/reviews/CPA-merge-<run_id>.json`, T040, follow the same contract): `schema` (the constant `review-verdict/1`), `verdict` (`GO` or `NO-GO`), `blocking_findings` (the count of blocking findings, 0 for a GO, as docs/16 §12.2.4 requires), `gate` (a gate id such as `G-GATE`, `G-PIN`, `G-DATA` or `G-AUDIT`, a work-package id, or, from contracts revision 16, a non-empty list of them: one verdict may release paths of several gated classes when its list holds every gate they require, CPA's S5 matching exact ids and counting a missing gate as a mismatch, T042), `covers_runs` (one entry per held commit the review covers: repository path, commit sha and `CPA-Run` id, read from the commit and its trailers; empty when it covers none, as for every review before CPA adoption, T047), the model and effort that performed it (plan owner's rule (e), rev 9), and, optionally, `accepted_pins` (one entry per pointer move the review accepts: the submodule path, the accepted sha and the move record that made it, a T435a or T435c op id or a CPA run id; read by the G-PIN reviews and pointer runs T441, T442, T580a and T581, and absent from a review that accepts no pin; at contracts revision 14 (`$FEAT/contracts/review-verdict.schema.json`; an `accepted_pins` sha is 40-hex, or null for a deleted submodule) the list is required on every GO whose `gate` is or includes `G-PIN` and may be empty when the review accepts no pointer move, the NO-GO-only field `refused_pins` lists the moves a NO-GO refuses, and a merge-review file that accepts a pointer move carries `for_verdict`, the verdict it serves, written as `$EV/reviews/<name>.json` or as the full path from the main repository root), on a GO whose gate list includes `G-GATE` and that the owner is to approve in `cpa-host` (T042, rev 32), `reviewed_files` (one entry per file of every `G-GATE` row that the review covers, the adoption verdict covering all of them of `scripts/repo/path_gates.tsv`: path from the main repository root and the file-content sha256, never a git blob id, a file that `scripts/repo/cpa_code.txt` names but the working tree lacks having no entry, round-23 review M7; T042, T046; a field that contracts revision 15 defines), the optional `findings[]`, each carrying its `finding_layer` (`source`, `artifact` or `runtime`, §11.4.226), and the optional `mutations[]` (reviewer- or author-authored, with operator, location and result, §11.4.194(6)(d)); a held commit is released only by a GO verdict committed in the main-repository HEAD whose `covers_runs` holds the commit's `CPA-Run` id, a GO only in a working tree or in a submodule's own tree releasing nothing (rule (a)); a GO verdict file is final: its `covers_runs` is written once, by ST-REV, in the version that first holds GO, listing every held commit that awaits that file at that time, which S5 checks over the unpushed range of every owned repository before it commits such a GO (20, `verdict_covers_incomplete`, naming the missing commit, T042), and a hold on a verdict file that holds GO, in the main-repository HEAD or in the same declared change set, or any change to such a file, is refused (20, `verdict_already_go`, rule (c), T042 S5), so work made after a GO waits on the file of a new review iteration (`-r<n>`) and an earlier GO never covers later work |
| `ST-xx` | work stream of docs/21 section 4.1 |
| `HC-n` | human checkpoint of docs/21 section 3.3; every record is written to `$EV/hc/HC-<n>[-<USn>].json` |
| `OD-nn` (open, ungrouped) | one of the 15 open `research.md` decisions of docs/21 section 8.6 that no ODG group covers; imported as its own `Operator-blocked` item (T070, T071) and named `BLOCKED-ON OD-nn` in the tasks of the work package it blocks, with the documented partial-proceed behaviour where one exists |

The per-phase-group convention blocks below add detail; where one of them names an abbreviation differently from this table, this table governs and the difference is a plan-review finding.

---

## Phase P0 Foundation

**Source**: docs/21 §3.3 (P0, P1), §4, §5.1, §5.2, §8, §10; detailed steps in docs/02, 04, 06, 11, 12, 15, 16, 19, 20.

**Phase-group conventions (P0-P1)**

- `$FEAT` = `specs/001-full-project-audit-remediation`; `$EV` = `$FEAT/evidence` (ledger, anchors, blobs, verdicts, docs/06 §11); `$AUD` = `$FEAT/audit`.
- `RUNP <IMG-ID> -- <cmd>` = `scripts/containers/run_pinned.sh <IMG-ID> -- <cmd>` (delivered by T007): resolves `<IMG-ID>` to `reference@sha256:<digest>` from `build/containers/images.lock.yaml`, runs rootless podman with `--userns=keep-id --cap-drop=ALL --memory --memory-swap --cpus --pids-limit --label project=catalogizer --label op_id=<id>`, `-v "$PWD":/src:ro -v <out>:/out:rw` (`<out>` from `--out <dir>`, default the ignored `.audit/out/<op_id>/`); refuses a tag-only or unresolved image; `--rw docs` adds `-v "$PWD/docs":/src/docs:rw`, the only writable source bind it accepts, for the register writes of `scripts/register/locked.sh` (T064).
- Every executable artifact is test-first (§11.4.224): the test task precedes the implementation task and the RED run is captured before code exists; every gate ships a paired §1.1 mutation that is observed failing before the gate is trusted (G-GATE).
- Until `tools/evidence/evrec` exists (WP-05), evidence is a transcript under `$EV/<wp>/` plus `$EV/<wp>/SHA256SUMS`; T095 (P0 exit gate) re-records every P0 transcript as an `ev/1` ledger entry (`$FEAT/contracts/evidence-record.schema.json`).
- Image-to-test binding: IMG-TESTUTIL (bash, git, sqlite3, python3 with `jsonschema`, `PyYAML` and `pytest`, jq) runs every P0 test that needs those tools; IMG-KCOV is kcov built on the IMG-TESTUTIL base (T006), so a coverage run also has git, jq and python3; IMG-SHELLCHECK only lints. T008 checks every (test, image) pair, not a union over images.
- Commit path: before CPA adoption is recorded (T047, after the T046 G-GATE GO), commits are plain commits on `main` integrated by the pre-adoption rule of CENTRAL C9 (d) (a fast-forward only under the rule stated there, otherwise a hand `git merge --no-ff` with HEAD as its first parent; never `--force`, never a rewrite); from T047 on every commit goes through `scripts/commit-push-all.sh` (docs/21 IC-16), started only as `cpa-host` (abbreviation table, rev 32), in commit windows (below). No commit lands on `main` before HC-0 (T014): docs/21 §3.3 makes plan acceptance at HC-0 the P0 entry; this list lets the read-only, preparation and test-first tasks start before T014 so that the owner request list (T013) exists to present at HC-0 (a recorded deviation), and every committing step of P0 depends on T014.
- Read-only `git`, CodeGraph CLI reads, Lumen read-only calls, the read-only verifier and the control-plane `podman run` launcher run on the host (docs/16 §5, §18), as do the build dispatcher `scripts/build/dispatch.sh`, the event hub `scripts/build/event_hub.sh`, the callback runner, their test `scripts/build/tests/test_dispatch_events.sh` (T005a, T005b) and the review provenance check of T094a, because they must run before any image exists and only orchestrate (they compile nothing; reason recorded with each task); everything that compiles, tests, lints, scans or renders runs in a pinned rootless container, and everything that compiles, builds an image or produces an artifact runs on the remote build host through the event-driven dispatcher (T005b, T121a), document rendering included: the HTML, PDF and DOCX exports and every other rendered document are produced by a remote render lane of IMG-DOCS and brought back verified, while the Markdown and CSV exports of the register (data written from the database, no render) and the documentation checks over the source stay local.
- `[REVIEW]` tasks are owned by stream ST-REV (Opus, xhigh, §11.4.209), never by the producing stream, iterated to zero blocking findings (§11.4.134), verdict files under `$EV/reviews/` in the review-verdict format of the abbreviation table (`covers_runs` included, empty for a review that covers no held commit); every review is started through the Workflow `agent()` path with Opus and `xhigh` set, and its provenance record (Workflow run id, model and effort read from the run record) is validated by T094a and enforced by T094d; a review whose effort could not be set records `?`, does not satisfy its gate and is never reported as `xhigh` (KC-P1); the provenance record of a verdict `$EV/reviews/<name>.json` is `$EV/reviews/<name>.provenance.json`, `<name>` the verdict's file name without `.json`, any `-r<n>` suffix included (`WP-04-r2.json` has `WP-04-r2.provenance.json`), the one form everywhere (rev 33); every `G-GATE` verdict carries `reviewed_files` listing the path and file-content sha256 of every `G-GATE` path held on it (`build/containers/images.lock.yaml`, a check's command file, its `scripts/repo/cpa_code.txt` line and its `scripts/repo/validate_checks.tsv` row among them), the list that `cpa-host --owner-trust approve` compares, an incomplete one refused with 20 `reviewed_files_incomplete` (CENTRAL C6).
- A path a P0-P1 task creates that does not exist at the plan commit is new and a deliverable of the task that names it, whether or not the text marks it `(new)` (same convention as the P4-P5 block).
- `BLOCKED-ON ODG-nn` means the step waits for the owner (docs/21 §8); a documented research.md default is named where one exists; a missing device, host, credential or service is recorded `blocked-unavailable` with its reason, never a pass (FR-025). `BLOCKED-ON OD-nn` does the same for the 15 open ungrouped decisions of docs/21 §8.6.
- ODG-34 (quota and budget) applies from P0 onward as a reversible working default under the docs/21 planning-rule-6 exception (docs/21 §8, "ODG-34 and ODG-35 in use"): at most 6 working agents, Sonnet as the default working model, Opus at xhigh for every review, the doc02 §13 budget rules. No `research.md` default backs it; it stays an `Operator-blocked` item the owner may overturn, and overturning it changes scheduling only, never an evidence rule.
- Disk headroom (§12.9; measured at plan review: root filesystem 96% used with 86 GB free, podman storage 76 GB): every `podman build`, `podman pull` and container run (RUNP, and the tasks that build or pull images: T006, T106-T113, T114, T143, T144, T149, T151, T211, T270) first runs `scripts/containers/disk_headroom.sh --op <op_id>` (T001), which reads the free bytes of the podman graphroot (`podman info --format '{{.Store.GraphRoot}}'`) and of the repository filesystem, refuses below the absolute byte threshold `min_free_bytes` in `scripts/containers/disk_headroom.conf` (never a percentage; derived from measured image sizes, T001) with reason `disk_below_headroom`, and records the before and after values in `$EV/disk/<op_id>.json`; every image this list builds carries `--label project=catalogizer`, and cleanup removes only images and containers with that label (`podman image prune --filter label=project=catalogizer`), never a global prune (§11.4.122).
- Tracked deviations (registered by T092, listed in the P0 and P1 exit records, never reported compliant): (a) retired in rev 13: the owner's C1 answer (T012a) removed the 'local containers only' option of ODG-07, so no local-build deviation exists: every build runs in a rootless container on the remote build host through the event-driven dispatcher (T005b, T121a), its artifacts brought back and verified by sha256 and digest (§11.4.108, §11.4.200) before use; the local host runs only control-plane steps and the `local` lanes of T121a in pinned images that were built remotely or pulled by digest; when no qualified build host is reachable a build step is `blocked-unavailable`, never run locally; the label (a) is kept so that older citations resolve; (b) §11.4.76 and §11.4.161 make the containers submodule the sole orchestration layer; RUNP and the runners compose `podman run` directly unless T002 finds a run primitive in `submodules/containers` to wrap, and the missing primitive is proposed upstream with T139 (§11.4.74); (c) the remote event emitter of the dispatcher lives in `scripts/build/remote/` until `submodules/containers` carries it (§11.4.74, §11.4.173: a missing build-container capability is added upstream), closed by T139.
- Event-driven build and test dispatch, zero waiting (owner decision C1, T012a; §11.4.173, §11.4.230, §11.4.232, §11.4.235): every task step that builds, compiles, runs `podman build` or produces an artifact (T006, T051, T106 to T113, T124, T141 to T144, T211, T241, T270, T443, T566 and the compiling lanes of T121a, whatever the task text says about where) is submitted through `scripts/build/dispatch.sh` (T005b) and returns at once; its completion, failure, timeout or host loss arrives as one authenticated `build-event/1` record consumed exactly once, which runs the step registered as its callback; no task polls a build or blocks on it, and the producing stream works on independent items (tests first, reviews, documentation, other lanes) while it runs, the fan-out bounded by the envelope (T119), the §12.6 60% memory ceiling, the §12.12 process headroom and the six-agent cap; a build with no completion inside its no-progress budget is `blocked-unavailable`, never a pass (the closed set of `blocked-unavailable` reasons of a dispatched build: `host_unreachable`, `no_qualified_host`, `build_liveness_lost`, `build_progress_flat`, `build_wallclock_exceeded`, `driver_secret_lost`, `artifact_unavailable` and, for a provenance-signing step, `signing_key_not_provisioned` of T446); the disk-headroom precondition of T001 (`scripts/containers/disk_headroom.sh`) runs on the build host for a remote build, and again on the local host before a brought-back image is loaded with `podman load` (its size as `--need`); a brought-back artifact is used only after `scripts/build/verify_artifact.sh` matches it to its event (§11.4.108); which steps are local is a closed, reviewed classification (T121b): only interpreter-only checks over the read-only source (bash, python3, jq and sqlite3 gates, `shellcheck`, `detect-secrets`, the `pre-commit-hooks` checks, `gofmt -l`, `goimports -l`, `prettier --check` and non-type-aware `eslint`) run locally, and every compile-class step (`go build`, `go vet`, `go test`, `tsc`, `vitest`, type-aware `eslint`, `cargo`, Gradle, image builds) runs remotely, the wrappers refusing it locally (T121b).
- Single writer (docs/04 §12.2): from T069 on, every mutating `$WI` or `sqlite3` command against `$DB` runs through `scripts/register/locked.sh` (T064), which runs it in IMG-TESTUTIL through `RUNP --rw docs`; read-only queries use the `immutable=1` URI (T071) only right after a checkpoint with no writer active, because that URI does not read rows still in the `-wal` file (docs/04 §12.2; reproduced in the round-10 review: 2 rows through `immutable=1` where `mode=ro` gave 3) and `mode=ro` cannot run on the read-only `/src` mount, where it would create `-shm` and `-wal` files: a read is either one `locked.sh` call that runs `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` and then the query, or a reader that refuses (20) while `docs/workable_items.db-wal` is non-empty.
- Repository-wide checks that fail on the current tree (the anti-bluff scan, revision headers, `check_pins.sh`, the QA bank validator) run as ratchets against their measured baselines under the bootstrap rule of the abbreviation table, never as whole-repository pass/fail stages that would refuse every commit; fixtures that violate such a check on purpose follow the deliberate-violation fixture convention of the same table (T040a). Whether one of these checks, or one of the plain checks taken from pre-commit, applies to a file at all is decided by its check class (abbreviation table, rule (V), T040b), never by an exemption written into a task. A plain check is not a ratchet: an existing file that already fails one when a task first declares it (measured in the round-10 review: `README.md` and `build-scripts/build-all.sh` lack a final newline, and `docker-compose.security.yml` has two trailing-whitespace lines and no final newline) is fixed by that task in the same change set and the fix named in its evidence (T036, T123, T148). The revision-header check is a ratchet that applies to every declared Markdown file whatever its row (T040; plan owner's decision after the round-11 reviews: a header is added when a file is next edited): a task that edits an existing tracked Markdown file without the §11.4.44 header adds it in the same change set, which lowers the file's baseline row (measured for rev 12: `README.md`, edited by T036, `.specify/memory/constitution.md`, edited by T081, and `docs/BUILD_CONTAINER_AUTO_DISPATCH.md`, edited by T122, carry none), except a file of class `generated` and a `docs/issues` ticket (class `legacy-collection`); an edited legacy root report drops its `legacy-collection` row in the same change set and gains the header (T040b).
- Every task that writes a `docs/scripts/*.md` companion adds its row to the index `docs/scripts/README.md` in the same change; T036 creates the index and lists the companions that exist when it runs.
- Commit windows (from T047 on; §11.4.84): the working tree is shared by every stream, and CPA refuses an uncommitted file that its declared change set does not name (13 at S7, 20 at the S0 sweep once T093 wires it), so commits are batched: at a window every stream stops writing, releases its long-op registrations and hands the conductor (ST-GOV) all of its uncommitted paths, each with the review verdict it still waits for, if any; the conductor runs CPA with their union as `--paths-from` (the stream of each path named in the commit message): the paths with no pending review form the first commit and are pushed, the paths still waiting for a review are committed after them as held commits (`Awaits-Review:`, T042) whose push waits until that verdict is committed in the main-repository HEAD with `verdict: GO` and the held commit's run in its `covers_runs` (review verdict row); work inside a submodule is committed only through a `CPA --repo <path>` run (a main-mode run refuses every declared path below a gitlink, held or not, with 20 `path_in_submodule`), its pointer moving later through G-PIN (T042, T042a); the paths of a G-GATE row of `scripts/repo/path_gates.tsv` (an entry of `build/containers/images.lock.yaml`, a check registration with its command file, its `scripts/repo/cpa_code.txt` line and its `scripts/repo/validate_checks.tsv` row, any other file `cpa_code.txt` names, such as `scripts/containers/run_pinned.sh`) are released only by a GO whose gate list includes `G-GATE`, and a gitlink only by one whose gate list includes `G-PIN` with its accepted sha (round-23 decision; contracts revision 16: `gate` is a gate id or a list of them, and one verdict may hold paths of several classes when its list holds every gate they require), so a work package that changes a gated path writes its own verdict with that gate in its list (for example `"gate": ["G-DATA", "G-GATE"]`); a separate `$EV/reviews/<WP>-gate.json` file that a task already names (T219 for T210 and T211; the P3 and P4 files of T288a, T307, T322a and T336a) stays valid, holding the paths its task names, but is never required, and a GO whose list lacks a gate that one of the net changes it releases requires is refused at S5 with 20 `verdict_gate_mismatch` (T042); the admission tables of T040b (`scripts/repo/fixture_roots.txt`, `scripts/repo/check_classes.tsv`, `scripts/repo/check_exemptions.tsv`, `scripts/repo/private_key_carriers.tsv`, `scripts/repo/exceptions.tsv` and the settings of `.secrets.baseline`) are no path-gate row and follow only T040b's held-table rule, under the verdict their header line names, whatever its gate (round-23 review M3); after every window the tracked tree is clean and no unreviewed change has reached a remote; a held commit also holds back the push of every later commit until its GO (S6, T042), so reviews of held work are scheduled first; a task that commits only after its review GO (for example T029) keeps that guarantee for the remotes: at an earlier window its in-flight paths become commits held on that review, and its commit step adds the rest together with the verdict; a clean-tree gate (T161, T225) runs right after a window; when an approved CPA release stops every run from committing (an approved check failing on every tree, a broken `scripts/repo/commit_recursive.sh`), the window is never forced through by hand: the owner recovery of CENTRAL C11 applies (the fixing GO approved uncommitted from the working tree with `--recovery`, its files then declared unheld by the next run). A review that ends in a NO-GO that abandons a held change: at the next window the producing stream runs `git revert --no-commit <held commits>`, `git revert --quit` and `git restore --staged -- <reverted paths>` (only the reverted content stays, unstaged, in the working tree; a plain `git revert` would make a trailer-less local commit that CPA refuses at S1 with 20, `unrecorded_local_commit`), and the conductor commits the reverted paths through CPA, declared and held on the same verdict file (never a history rewrite, §11.4.113; this procedure governs the P4-P5 bullet of the same rule and docs/16 §12.2.4); when a reverted `--repo` commit moved gitlinks, the revert run is made with `CPA --reverting <held commits>`, and CPA itself settles them with `record_pending_pin.sh --settle-nested <path> <old HEAD> <new HEAD> --reverting --in-hold <run_id> --out $CPA_RUN/settle/` and makes the pending-row decision of T042a (the conductor never calls the helper); ST-REV then writes a GO into that verdict file whose `covers_runs` names the held commits and the revert commit and states that the net change pushed is none; S5 judges that GO net per path against the released commit (T042, round-23 review B1), so a reverted pin move needs no `accepted_pins` entry for the refused sha, which no remote holds, and a GO with an empty `accepted_pins` (or with no `G-PIN` at all) releases both; that GO releases both, while a GO that names the held commits without the revert is refused at S5 before it is committed (20, `verdict_covers_incomplete`, review verdict row), so the abandoned change never reaches a remote without its revert and a NO-GO never blocks the pushes of `main` for good (T039 fixtures; this held form is the one NO-GO form of this plan for a held commit that is not a merge). A NO-GO on a held CPA merge commit (round-24 review I1; its merge-review file `$EV/reviews/CPA-merge-<run_id>.json`) is never answered by a plain revert of the merge, because `git revert` of a merge commit needs `-m 1` and the net change of the merge is the foreign content, never none: (i) a rejected conflict resolution is replaced by a corrective commit that the conductor declares at the next window, held on that same merge-review file, its content the resolution the reviewer requires, written by the Opus-xhigh resolver (§11.4.211); (ii) rejected foreign content is taken out by `git revert -m 1 --no-commit <merge>`, then `git restore --source=HEAD --staged --worktree -- <every path the revert changed that the NO-GO did not reject>`, `git revert --quit` and `git restore --staged -- <rejected paths>`, so only the reverted content of the rejected paths stays, unstaged, and the conductor commits those paths through CPA held on the same merge-review file; in both cases ST-REV then writes a GO into that merge-review file whose `covers_runs` names the merge run and the corrective run, which approves the corrective content, and whose gate list holds every gate S5 requires for the net change from the released commit that the merge and the corrective commit leave (`G-GATE` while a G-GATE path stays changed and not exempt, `G-PIN` with its accepted entries while a gitlink does), never a 'net none' GO: a GO that lacks such a gate gives 20 `verdict_gate_mismatch` or `verdict_pins_incomplete`, and one that names the merge run without the corrective run 20 `verdict_covers_incomplete` (T039 fixtures, T043 mutations, T045). When a remote of the main repository moved while a held commit waits, CPA integrates the moved tip by a merge commit of its own, held on its own merge-review file `$EV/reviews/CPA-merge-<run_id>.json`, never by a rebase (T040, T042), and until that file releases it S6 pushes nothing below the merge to any remote (T041); in P0 to P2, ST-REV reviews every such file before the next window (Opus at xhigh: the merge brings in only the remote's commits and keeps every held change, and a resolved conflict is reviewed under §11.4.211) and writes GO with the merge run in its `covers_runs`, its gate list including `G-GATE` when the merge brings in a change to a G-GATE path by a commit that is not a CPA commit reviewed for `G-GATE` (T042 predicate, round-25 review B1) or resolves a conflict in one, and `G-PIN` with its accepted entries when it brings in a gitlink no remote tip records (T042 S5, round-23 review I4, M2), which the conductor declares in the next window's change set beside the held commits' own verdicts; in P3, T307 does it with G-AUDIT; so a foreign push that changes no path of the window's change set never stops the windows. One that does change such a path while the path holds an uncommitted change gives 12 (`ff_blocked_by_local_changes`) on every run until it is integrated, `--local-only` included, because S1 always runs; the remediation is to re-run the window with `--commit-before-integrate` (T042; plan owner's decision after the round-11 reviews): under the lock and after the §9.2 backup, CPA commits the declared change set as ordinary CPA commits, held where declared, and then runs the merge path, so the overlap becomes a merge, clean or a `merge_conflict` that a `--resolve-merge` run resolves; a hand commit (20, `unrecorded_local_commit`), a stash (13) or parking the edit and restoring it over the remote's change is never the remediation. Chained and binary stores, `$EV/ledger.jsonl`, `$EV/flake_ledger.jsonl`, `$EV/anchors.jsonl` and `$EV/deferrals.jsonl` (hash-chained or append-only lines) and `docs/workable_items.db` with its dump and exports, have a single writer: the stream that owns the store, writing it only in the conductor's checkout through the store's own tool (ST-QA through `tools/evidence/evrec`, the deferral tools of WP-05 and `scripts/qa/stress_new_tests.sh` of T563; ST-REG through `scripts/register/locked.sh` of WP-06), so a clone of another actor never writes them; a merge conflict in one of them is never resolved textually: because it means that a second writer broke this rule, its remediation starts with a question to the plan owner (§11.4.66), and the owning stream then re-records its local side on top of the remote side through that tool's re-record mode into the refused run's `.audit/merge-resolution/<run_id>/`, `tools/evidence/evrec rerecord` for the evidence stores (T050; its seq map renumbers the `ledger#<seq>` references, which `evrec remap-refs` rewrites in a change set held on the same merge-review verdict) and `scripts/register/replay.sh` for the register (T067a), which `integrate_merge.sh` checks before it commits the merge (20, `store_not_rerecorded`, T040).
- Container outputs: a containerized step writes only to `/out` (RUNP `--out <dir>`, default the ignored `.audit/out/<op_id>/`, T003); a host step copies each file the task keeps to its tracked path (under `$EV`, `$AUD` or the source tree) and records the source and destination sha256 in its `ev/1` entry, or in its `SHA256SUMS` line before the recorder exists; no container writes `/src`, except `scripts/register/locked.sh` through `RUNP --rw docs` (T064).
- New and edited Markdown files: every tracked `*.md` file a task creates or edits (evidence notes and `docs/scripts/*.md` companions included) carries the §11.4.44 revision header table (rows `Revision`, `Created`, `Last modified`, `Status`) in its first 40 lines, because the S3 revision-header check (T040) applies to every declared Markdown file, so it meets no new key and an edited legacy file gains its header in the change set that lowers its row; a file that a generator writes in the bold-line form `**Revision:**` and `**Last modified:**` (the register engine's export, T067) passes as well, and a file of a class to which the revision-header check does not apply (class `generated`, for example the engine's exports, and class `legacy-collection`, the `docs/issues` tickets and the legacy root reports until an edit drops a report's row; check class row, T040b) is exempt through its class, never through a list kept by a task.
- Central decisions C1 to C12 (revised in rev 35): each is defined once, in T042, in its contiguous paragraph labelled `CENTRAL Cn (definition)` (C1 the tables rule with the pending exit, C2 the cancel of a suspended run, C3 the T039 fixture harness and its trust state, C4 the empty hooks directory, C5 the `cpa-host` modes `--check-provenance`, `--exec-approved`, `reanchor` and `revoke`, C6 the `approve` refusals, C7 the owed approvals, C8 the direct calls through `--exec-approved`, C9 the first-parent and root rule, C10 the build-event hub in the adoption set with its identity stamp and its scoped candidates, C11 the owner recovery from a defective CPA release, C12 the commit-turn holder pid); every citation in this file, "central decision Cn", "CENTRAL Cn" or a bare `Cn` beside a CPA term, names that definition and restates nothing that differs from it; the owner's answers recorded by T012a ("owner decision C1", "the owner's C1 answer", "the owner's C2 answer") are a different series and never one of these.

a non-zero exit ends in `failed` with the reason, never a silent retry; Every competing terminal path (`cancel`, a consumed `completed`, the liveness owner, host loss, secret loss) resolves through that same rename, never by a rename that overwrites a file; the losers record themselves `superseded` in their own journal line, and a `completed` event consumed after a `cancel` won never runs a callback for the cancelled build. a group not sealed within its group budget, or sealed with no member, is reported by the sweep as `group_orphaned` and made terminal `cancelled`; a member that completed, whatever its `exit_class` (`succeeded`, `test_failed`, `build_failed`), is a finished member and never ends the group early, so a GREEN x3 or a flake run with one failing iteration still completes all its iterations; each member's callback is a record-only no-op, and the group has one callback, registered once, claimed by the same rename of a prepared `.audit/builds/group/<group_id>/terminal` directory (the parent folder `.audit/builds/group/` is created, mode 0700, by the first `submit` of a group; a CPA run then gives `remote_check_unavailable`, T121b), and the group terminal records every member's kind. ## Phase P1 Containerized infrastructure

Remote-host rule (stated once, round-23 review): every step of P1 and P2 that builds or runs on a remote build host (the image builds of T106, the D-01..D-04 RED builds of T107 and T108 and fix builds of T109 to T113, the measurement of T115, T141, T143, T144, T211, and every `remote` or `split` TIC lane) is BLOCKED-ON ODG-07 (input, cannot be defaulted) until HC-1b (T102) records the host; the explicit marks on T141, T143, T144, T147 and T155 restate this rule and add nothing to it; T203 and T204 (rev 24 decision; FR-025, §11.4.3 SKIP-with-reason, partial proceed) do not wait for the T143 and T144 image builds or for ODG-29: a leg that cannot run is recorded `blocked-unavailable` in its baseline file, so T208 and the P2 exit T220 wait only for what they already reach through T006a, T106 (via T200a) and T211. Terminal-state rule for the owner-input legs of P1 (round-24 review I1): T143 and T144 (ODG-29 for the Android fallback) and the NFS leg (ODG-08, T134 and T134a) each end in a recorded terminal state, `built` (or `pass`) with its evidence, or `blocked-unavailable` / `blocked` naming the reason and the decision (`no_qualified_host`, `host_unreachable`, `odg29_agp_unbuildable`, `odg08_unanswered`), written to its record file and owed to that decision's register item; a task whose record is `blocked` completes, so the WP-13 and WP-14 reviews (T136, T147) and the P1 exit (T159) wait only for the record, never for the owner's answer; a dependent that needs the built image (T155, the IMG-RUST tasks of P3) reads the record and stays blocked while it is not `built`.

G-GATE holds in this slice (contracts rev 16): a review verdict's `gate` field is a string or an array; one verdict may hold paths of several classes provided its gate list includes each required gate (a gitlink needs G-PIN; a `cpa_code` path, `build/containers/images.lock.yaml` or any other G-GATE row of `scripts/repo/path_gates.tsv` needs G-GATE). Every G-GATE path a task of this slice changes is therefore held on its work package's own verdict, named in the task, and that verdict's gate list includes G-GATE; a registration or table row committed after that verdict's GO is held on a new iteration `<verdict>-r<n>.json` (an unheld G-GATE path is refused `path_gate_unheld`, a hold on a verdict already GO is refused `verdict_already_go`, T042). The check tables of `scripts/repo/` that T040b governs (`scripts/repo/fixture_roots.txt` among them) are not `path_gates.tsv` rows; a row change to one of them follows the T040b held-table rule on the same verdict as the change it serves.

**Exit (doc21 §3.3)**: `SELECT count(*) FROM v_unmapped_entries` returns 0 and the doc04 §13.1 per-source totals show `entries = mapped` for every `reg_sources` row (docs/21 IC-39: the docs/03 staging query on `src_entry ... disposition='PENDING'` names a table the docs/04 v4 DDL does not have; there the entries live in `reg_source_entries` and the 'no PENDING entry' rule is this view); every source row mapped with its `reg_source_map.relation` in the closed set; every docs/21 §9.1 seed and every §9.5 entry a mapped source entry; every external tracker recorded `queried` or `skipped(reason)`; `applicability.yaml` with no `?` cell; coverage baseline per application recorded. **Human checkpoint HC-2** (T222, `$EV/hc/HC-2.json`): SC-001 reconciliation reviewed; ODG-09 legacy-closure policy and doc04 D-6 category mapping confirmed; the reviewed exit record `$EV/p2-exit.json` (T220, T221) precedes it.

**Phase-group conventions (P2-P3)** (abbreviations only, no new mechanism):
- `$EV` = `specs/001-full-project-audit-remediation/evidence/` (doc06 §11 layout); every PASS/FAIL below is an `ev/1` entry in `$EV/ledger.jsonl` written by the recorder `tools/evidence/evrec` (WP-05), validated against `$FEAT/contracts/evidence-record.schema.json`.
- `$WI` = `submodules/constitution/scripts/workable-items/bin/workable-items`; `$DB` = `docs/workable_items.db` (ODG-11 default, OD-11). Items are created only through the pre-minted `reg_ids` path of doc04 §12.3 step 1, and every mutating `$WI` or `sqlite3` command runs through `scripts/register/locked.sh` (T064), including the minting of `FND-NNNN` ids by the P3 agents, of which up to six run at once.
- "runner(IMG-x)" = the WP-12 container runner wrapper for image IMG-x (rootless podman, digest from `build/containers/images.lock.yaml`, `--memory` and `--pids-limit` set, `jobs=1` until per-job memory is measured, doc16 §8.2). Its exact script path is fixed by WP-12: `scripts/containers/run_<toolchain>.sh` (T120) and the lane dispatcher `scripts/test-in-container.sh <app> <lane> -- <cmd>` (TIC, T121); no task here invents another. Git, index reads and the read-only verifier run on the host (doc16 §18); nothing builds or tests on the bare host (§11.4.173).
- Gate scripts: `scripts/register/gate.sh` (doc04 §12.3 step 2; `--completion` mode for step 3, T180); exports through `scripts/register/export.sh` and `reconcile.sh` (T067). The disk-headroom precondition, the tracked deviations, the ratchet rule, the commit windows, the container-output rule and the new-Markdown header rule of the P0-P1 conventions apply here unchanged. Commits only through `scripts/commit-push-all.sh` (WP-04, IC-16) in commit windows, on `main`, fast-forward to every upstream, never force; with up to six P3 agents writing at once, each stream's uncommitted files wait for the next window, and a clean-tree gate (T161, T225) runs right after one.
- File names marked "(new)" are proposed here where the source document names the tool but not its path; the reviewer of the WP confirms the path. Every other path a P2-P3 task creates that does not exist at the plan commit is likewise new and a deliverable of the task that names it, mark or no mark.
- `[REVIEW]` tasks are owned by stream ST-REV on Opus at xhigh (§11.4.209), never by the producing stream (§11.4.240); every verdict file follows the review-verdict row of the abbreviation table (`covers_runs` included).
- Audit patches in remote lanes (rev 19): a P3 task that applies a recorded patch (`$AUD/patches/<task>.patch`, for example T229, T238, T249, T292, T293) ships the patch in the snapshot of its lane (an untracked or declared file of the shipped tree), the remote command applies it to a copy inside the build container, never to the shipped tree, and the patch's sha256 enters the argv digest, so `AUD-001` and `AUD-002` run the same purpose key except its iteration id and stay comparable.
- Compile-class runner and TIC calls (rev 15; owner decision C1, T121a, T121b): every `runner(IMG-x)` or `TIC` call of P2-P3 whose image is of class `compile` (IMG-GO, IMG-NODE build lanes, IMG-RUST, IMG-ANDROID, IMG-MUT, IMG-PW; for example T201, T229, T239, T245, T255 and T258) is a remote lane submitted through T121a with its purpose key, a lane that needs the WP-13 stack being a split lane (remote compile, local run of the verified binaries, the web e2e run half in IMG-PW through its reviewed run-half row against the `runtime`-class web image); its RED and its GREEN x3 are taken from the callback records of the long-op registry (T089a), three iterations being three builds; RUNP refuses a local compile-class command (T121b), so no P2-P3 task runs one locally, whatever its text says.
- Audit work reaches no remote before G-AUDIT (rev 9): from T225 until the WP-39R GO verdicts are committed (T307), every path of WP-30 to WP-39 that a commit window takes is a held commit: audit records (`$AUD/`, `$EV/` and the register writes of P3) on `$EV/reviews/WP-39R.json` and code, tests and configuration on `$EV/reviews/WP-39R-code.json` (T306), except the WP-37 tooling that T287 has reviewed (T288 commits it after that GO); a held commit holds back the push of every later commit (S6, T042), so pushes of `main` wait for G-AUDIT, which is scheduled right after WP-39; when another clone pushes `main` in that period, the next window's CPA run integrates the moved tip by a merge commit held on its own merge-review file `$EV/reviews/CPA-merge-<run_id>.json` (rule (Y), T042), which does not stop the windows while the push changes no path of the window's change set, and a push that does is integrated by re-running the window with `--commit-before-integrate` (P0-P1 conventions, T042), and ST-REV reviews those merge files together with G-AUDIT, so the T307 push needs their GO verdicts as well.

### WP-20 Source freeze, enumeration, import (stream ST-REG, size XL, FR-001 FR-002 FR-003, SC-001)

Source: doc03 §10 steps 0-10, §15; doc04 §9 stages 0-3, §13; doc12 WP-Q5 and §11; docs/21 §9.1, §9.5 and §12.4. Depends on WP-06 and a frozen commit. Owner decisions: ODG-17 for the category mapping (T168, T223) and ODG-39 for the disposition of each docs/21 §9.5 entry (T224); the enumeration and import proceed without either.

- [ ] T161 [US1] Step 0 freeze, right after a commit window: before this task writes anything, measure the clean tracked tree (abbreviation table: `scripts/repo/verify_repos.sh --no-remote` with `summary.dirty` equal to `summary.dirty_excepted`, pending pin moves listed) and refuse to continue on a tree that is not clean (doc02 §12.1 `dirty:false`); before that measurement, refuse to measure while a CPA run of the repository is suspended (round-34 review m3; the clean-tree rule of T121b, whose `suspend_writes.json` paths may still be written): the `commit_push` holder is read as T090 reads it, through `cpa-host --exec-approved scripts/longops/holder.sh commit_push`, and a holder of kind `suspended-run` in any state (live, `ready_to_resume` or `expired`) refuses with `run_suspended` naming its run id, nothing written (remediation: the run's `--resume`, or the S0 `--expire` of the next commit window's CPA run for an expired holder, T088), any non-zero exit of that call, `project_not_trusted` included, refusing with `holder_unread`; fixtures, on the CENTRAL C3 harness with a scratch longops registry built as T088's holder fixtures build it: a `suspended-run` holder reported live, one reported `ready_to_resume` and one reported `expired` are each refused `run_suspended` with nothing written, the harness with its trust state removed (the holder call refused `project_not_trusted`) is refused `holder_unread` with nothing written, and the clone with no holder passes the check; RED: run before the check exists, the live `suspended-run` fixture is not refused, captured to `$EV/register/freeze-suspended-red.txt`; GREEN x3; paired mutation: a freeze copy that skips the holder read lets the live fixture through, so it FAILs, recorded in `$EV/register/freeze-suspended-mutation.txt`; then on the host record `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git submodule status --recursive`, that measurement and the CPA run record of the run that made HEAD (abbreviation table: its report sha256, or `null` with a reason) through `tools/evidence/evrec` into `$EV/register/freeze.json`. Frozen snapshot (round-24 review I6; round-27 review B1): on the host, materialise the frozen commit read-only as `.audit/freeze/<sha>/` (ignored, never tracked) by `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<absolute path of a scratch index outside the repository> git read-tree <sha>` then `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<same index> git checkout-index -a --prefix=<toplevel>/.audit/freeze/<sha>/` (`<toplevel>` = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, absolute, round-28 review I1), never `git archive` (measured on HEAD 2e64a185, 2026-10-04: `git archive` honours `export-ignore` and the repository uses it, `.specify/extensions/superspec/.gitattributes` dropping 24 tracked paths from the archive, while `checkout-index` wrote all 4905 blob entries; neither writes a file for a gitlink, `git archive` emitting an empty directory entry and `checkout-index` an empty directory); snapshot and listing use the SAME recursive submodule set, built from RECORDED shas only (round-28 review I2): the walk starts at the mode-`160000` entries of `git -c core.quotepath=false ls-tree -r -z <sha>` and descends into each submodule's RECORDED commit (`git -C <abs submodule path> -c core.quotepath=false ls-tree -r -z <recorded sha>`), never its checked-out commit, so a nested entry is the gitlink its parent's recorded commit holds (97 entries at that commit, 44 of them top-level, nested ones by their full root-relative path), whatever source class it holds; decision: the freeze always materialises the recorded sha and never refuses a pending pin move (T042a and G-PIN create them by design and the clean measurement above admits them): an entry whose `git submodule status --recursive` line has the prefix `+` is recorded in `freeze.json` as `pending_pins` (path, recorded sha, checked-out sha), and the top-level entries of that path list (gitlinks of the superproject's own tree) must equal the top-level entries of the measurement's pending pin moves, a difference refusing `freeze_pending_pin_mismatch` naming each; a nested `+` entry is taken from `git submodule status --recursive` itself, the same instrument that defines the prefix, recorded in `pending_pins` and compared with nothing else (round-29 review, UNCONFIRMED there: whether `verify_repos.sh` lists nested pending pins; the top-level restriction makes the check independent of that); every entry is materialised from that submodule's own object store with ABSOLUTE paths only (round-28 review I1: under `git -C` a relative `--prefix` or a relative `GIT_INDEX_FILE` resolves against the submodule's work tree; measured 2026-10-04 in a scratch repository, `--prefix=out/sub/` given with `-C sub` wrote `sub/out/sub/f`, and a relative index file was created in `sub/`), as `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<absolute scratch index outside the repository, one per entry> git -C <abs submodule path> read-tree <recorded sha>` then `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<same index> git -C <abs submodule path> checkout-index -a --prefix=<toplevel>/.audit/freeze/<sha>/<submodule path>/`, `<abs submodule path>` being `<toplevel>/<submodule path>`; before the two calls `git -C <abs submodule path> rev-parse --show-toplevel` must print `<abs submodule path>` (an uninitialised, empty directory resolves to the enclosing repository instead) and `git -C <abs submodule path> cat-file -e <recorded sha>^{commit}` must exit 0: an uninitialised entry (status prefix `-`, or that toplevel check failing) or a recorded sha absent from its object store refuses the freeze with `freeze_submodule_unmaterialisable` naming it, and a non-zero exit of `git submodule status --recursive` (for example a gitlink with no `.gitmodules` mapping: `fatal: no submodule mapping found`, rc 128, measured 2026-10-04 in a scratch repository) refuses `freeze_submodule_status_failed` with its stderr; then `chmod -R a-w` (it does not follow a symlink met in the traversal: measured 2026-10-04, a link inside the tree to a file outside it left that file's mode unchanged); record in `freeze.json` the snapshot path and a manifest (path, sha256 of every regular file and symlink, a symlink hashed as the sha256 of its `readlink` target string (no trailing newline) and never followed (round-28 review I3: dangling links are tracked in the submodules, measured 2026-10-04 by `find submodules -xtype l`: `submodules/helix_qa/tools/opensource/kiwi-tcms/tcms/locale/sr_Latn`, 8 under `submodules/helix_qa/tools/opensource/unstructured/scripts/performance/`, and `submodules/constitution/scripts/fastcycle/tests/fixtures/resume_revalidate/rr_r6_dangling_symlink_dep/tree_current/dep_a/broken_link`; `sha256sum` of a dangling link fails and of a live absolute link reads outside the read-only snapshot), which is the sha256 of the bytes `git cat-file blob` prints for that mode-`120000` entry, and every P2 re-hash against the manifest (`freeze_snapshot_moved`, below) applies the same rule; directories, the empty gitlink directories included, are not manifest entries) with its own sha256; because the snapshot carries no `.git` (round-25 review I3), the two git-derived listings the enumerations need are taken on the host at freeze time and recorded with it: the tracked-file listing, FILES ONLY: the entries of `git -c core.quotepath=false ls-tree -r -z <sha>` (and, for every submodule of that same recursive set, `git -C <abs submodule path> -c core.quotepath=false ls-tree -r -z <recorded sha>` with its path prefix) whose mode is `100644`, `100755` or `120000`, path only, written to `.audit/freeze/<sha>.files.txt` with its sha256 in `freeze.json` (round-29 review I1: every `ls-tree` call of this task, the walk included, uses `-z`, and the path is the bytes of each NUL-terminated record after its first TAB, never a newline-split line: without `-z` git C-quotes a path holding a byte above 0x7f, a TAB or a newline, and `core.quotepath=false` alone still quotes TAB and newline; measured 2026-10-04: the recorded commit `4d37b88b` of `submodules/helix_qa/tools/opensource/midscene` holds `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/llm-connectivity-issue---模型连接错误.md`, which plain `ls-tree -r` prints as `".github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/llm-connectivity-issue---\346\250\241...\257.md"` and `ls-tree -r -z` prints byte-identical to the name on disk, and in a scratch repository `-c core.quotepath=false ls-tree -r` printed a file named `a<newline>b` as `"a\nb"`; the listing file holds the raw path bytes, each path followed by one NUL byte and no newline, and every consumer (T164, T166, T167, T174) splits it on NUL (`xargs -0 <cmd> --`, `grep -z`, or a split on `b'\0'`), never by lines, and every command that receives listing paths as arguments gets `--` before them (or each path prefixed `./`), because a path beginning with `-` is otherwise parsed as an option (round-30 review m5; ## Phase P3: Audit pass (doc21 §3.3 P3, §5.4)

**Entry**: P1 detectors pinned with needles (WP-15); index gate PASS in the current pass; register accepting findings. **Parallelism**: up to six read-only audit agents, one per unit (doc02 §14.3 waves W1-W3); heavy local-site detectors queued at K = min(floor(18 GiB / measured peak RSS), 4) (remote lanes are bounded by the build host's envelope, T005a (l)); one Android container at a time; `ulimit -u` headroom checked before each wave (§12.12). **Exit**: every unit has a recorded audit result; second run from an identical manifest yields `IDENTICAL` (SC-002); every finding carries location, severity, category, evidence and register link (FR-007). **HC-3**: owner accepts the audit report. Every detector has golden-good, golden-bad and a control needle before any zero result is trusted (doc06 §10, §11.4.201(7)(b)). Each finding is a `finding/1` record (`$FEAT/contracts/finding.schema.json`) with an `FND-NNNN` id minted from `reg_ids` through `scripts/register/locked.sh`, written once as `$AUD/findings/<FND-NNNN>.json` (the finding store of doc02 §9 and data-model); a later run that finds the same `fingerprint` appends its run id to that file's `run_ids` and mints nothing (§11.4.214). The per-run `$AUD/runs/<run-id>/findings.index.jsonl` is a derived projection (doc02 §9): one line per finding with `unit`, `path`, `line_start`, `rule_id` and `fingerprint`, sorted by `(unit, path, line_start, rule_id)`, with no timestamps, no `run_ids` and no minted id, so two runs on identical input give byte-identical index files (SC-002). The disk-headroom precondition and the single-writer rule of the P0-P1 conventions apply to every P3 container run and register write.

**Audited input of the two audit runs (SC-002; decided in rev 9, replacing the UNCONFIRMED note that rev 8 placed in T300; docs/21 IC-47 withdrew the docs/02 §12.1 rev 5 exclusion list and left the question open).** `AUD-001` and `AUD-002` audit one input, the input commit that T225 records (the main-repository HEAD right after the commit window that opens P3) together with the submodule commits its gitlinks record, identified by `input_tree`: per repository, the sha256 of the sorted `git ls-tree -r <commit>` lines of the paths that exist at the input commit and lie outside the excluded paths of `$AUD/input-exclusions.txt`, computed by `scripts/audit/input_tree.sh` (T225) for the input commit and, at the start of `AUD-002`, for the current HEAD. The exclusion list is written in T225 before `AUD-001` starts, is not changed until `AUD-002` ends (its sha256 is in both manifests) and is reviewed in T303; it names the audit's own outputs (`$AUD/`, `$EV/`, `docs/workable_items.db`, `docs/register/`), the plan set `$FEAT/`, and the existing files that P3 tasks are allowed to change: `scripts/repo/validate_checks.tsv` (T283a), `scripts/repo/fixture_roots.txt` (T235), `docs/scripts/README.md` (T248a, T283a), and `docs/DOC_SCOPE.yaml`, `docs/reference/evidence/` and `docs/security/rotation-ledger.md` where they exist at the input commit (T265, T281, T282, T286), and the two gate-class files that P3 tasks edit, `scripts/repo/cpa_code.txt` (T288, the T283a command file) and `build/containers/images.lock.yaml` (the image entries of T291, T277b and any other P3 task; next block, item (4)). A file that a P3 task creates is not part of the input, because only paths of the input commit count. `main_head` is recorded in both manifests but not compared, so a commit window during P3 leaves the audited input unchanged as long as it changes no input path. Every detector takes its unit's file set from `git ls-tree -r --name-only <input commit>` limited to the unit's paths and the input, never from a working-tree glob, so a file a P3 task creates belongs to no unit (T306 reviews it); the link crawler treats a link into an excluded path as external and does not read its target. An audit step that has to change an input file, or add a file inside an application or module tree that a detector builds or tests as a whole directory (`catalog-api`, `catalog-web`, the Tauri and Android trees, the submodules), never does so in the working tree during P3: it applies the change as a patch `$AUD/patches/<task>.patch` to a scratch copy of the unit (the doc08 §6.1 writable-copy pattern), `AUD-002` applies the same patch set (each patch's sha256 in both manifests; class `patches` of rule (V), T040b: a patch is committed byte-exact, its blank context lines being single spaces, so the whitespace and end-of-file checks do not apply to it), and the change reaches the source tree only after `AUD-002`, through T302 (held on the T306 code review); this binds T229, T238, T249, T292 and T293 and any other P3 task in the same position. Every unit result records the image digests and the sha256 of each tooling file its detectors ran (`tooling`), and a unit whose listed tooling changed after its `AUD-001` result is re-run under `AUD-001` before T300, so both runs of every unit use the same tooling. T299 checks that every path changed since the input commit (`git diff --name-only <input commit> HEAD` and the uncommitted files) is an excluded path or a path added after the input commit outside every application and module tree; T300 refuses to start while `input_tree` differs. Because the detectors read checkouts while `input_tree` hashes committed trees, both runs also fix the checkouts (rev 10, round-9 review): T225 and T300 require, in the clean-tree measurement of every input repository, no pointer drift and no row of `.audit/pending_pins.tsv` (`summary.pin_drift` 0, so each checkout's HEAD equals the gitlink the input commit records), and each manifest records, as an identity field, the sha256 of every file of an excepted dirty row of `scripts/repo/exceptions.tsv` (the docling case), so a checkout that differs from the hashed trees, or excepted dirt that changes between the runs, makes the manifests differ. A commit window during P3 that has to integrate a remote move does so by a CPA merge commit (P2-P3 conventions); its incoming changes reach the audited input only when they change an input path, which T299 and the `input_tree` comparison then report. This design is presented to the plan owner with the plan at HC-0 (T013, T014; docs/21 IC-47 leaves the state vector to the plan owner), and docs/02 §12.1, §12.2 and §20 (rev 7) and docs/21 IC-47, §12.2 and §12.10 (rev 11) are reconciled to this block.

**Unit partition, index route, registry snapshots and gate-class holds (round-22 review; FR-005, FR-006, SC-002).** (1) Unit partition: T225 writes `$AUD/unit-partition.tsv` (one row per path glob from the repository root, giving a unit id or `excluded` with its reason), fixed like the exclusion list until `AUD-002` ends, its sha256 an identity field of both manifests; `scripts/audit/unit_partition.sh` (new, T225) maps every path of `git ls-tree -r --name-only <input commit>` of the main repository to exactly one row (a gitlink is one path, mapped to its own-organisation repository's unit, the one third-party direct submodule, `submodules/superspec` (upstream `WangX0111/superspec`), to an `excluded` row naming T259 and T269) under one precedence rule, as in T040b: rows are git-wildmatch globs from the repository root (`*` stays inside one directory, `**/` matches zero or more directories), a row that names an exact path (no glob character) takes precedence over every glob row, and a path that no row matches, or that glob rows of two different units (or of a unit and `excluded`) match with no exact-path row, FAILs with the path and the matching rows named; it writes `$AUD/unit-map.tsv`; the units are the application units (`catalog-api`, `catalog-web`, `catalogizer-api-client` (T240a), `catalogizer-desktop`, `installer-wizard`, `catalogizer-android`, `catalogizer-androidtv`), one unit per own-organisation repository of `$AUD/submodules.tsv` (T017; the set that the T259 roster re-derives and must equal), the eight WP-36 units (the six of doc02 §8.6-8.8, `OCU-CUDA-Sidecar/**`, `qa-ai-system/**`, `Website/**`, `Build/**`, `scripts/**` with `build-scripts/**`, the root compose files `docker-compose*.yml` (T272, T273) and `tools/**` (the evidence tooling `tools/evidence/*` that P0 creates; `tools/audit/**` and `tools/perf/**` are created in P3, are no input path and get no row, block (5)), and `tests/**` with the bank trees `challenges/helixqa-banks/**`, `challenges/data/**` and `challenges/results/**` (bank entries checked with the T210 validator in T276), plus `examples/helixcode-qa-integration/**` (T277a) and the deployment-and-configuration unit (T277b), whose rows are explicit globs and exact paths, never a glob over `*.sh` across the tree (which would also match `qa-ai-system/scripts/**`, `tests/*.sh` and `.specify/**`): `deployment/**`, `deploy/**` (`infra-compose.yml` and `infra-compose-test.yml`, also checked by T273), `docker/**`, `config/**`, `monitoring/**`, `database/**`, `sonarqube/**`, `challenges/scripts/*.sh`, `Upstreams/*.sh`, the root shell script `commit` (no `.sh` suffix) with the `env.properties` it sources, the root configuration files `config.json`, `firebase.json`, `.firebaserc`, `gradle.properties`, `versions.json`, `sonar-project.properties`, `dependency-check-suppressions.xml` and `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, the root scanner configurations `.gosec.json`, `.semgrep.yml`, `.snyk.json`, `.trivy.yaml`, `.trivy-secrets.yaml`, `.trivyignore`, `.nancy-ignore` and `.gitleaksignore`, the root `.env.*` files, the three committed runtime files `frontend.pid`, `server2.pid` and `server3.pid`, and the files that P0-P2 tasks create under the lowercase `build/` tree, as exact-path rows `build/containers/images.lock.yaml`, `build/hosts.env` and `build/components.json` plus the glob `build/**` for any other file there (git-wildmatch is case-sensitive: `build/**` never matches `Build/**`, which stays the `build` unit, round-25 review I2), and the root configuration files `codegraph.json`, `.mcp.json` and `.secrets.baseline` (each parsed by T277b (e);
