## Phase P4: Contract layer (docs/21 §3.3 P4, §5.5)

**Entry**: WP-30 backend audit accepted at G-AUDIT (WP-39R GO); WP-13 real-service stack running; WP-05 evidence recorder available.
**Exit**: contract inventory CT-1..CT-22 (docs/01 §14) each with a test on both sides or a recorded n/a, the named test paths proven present in the reviewed commit by T335a and a pending n/a carried as an open owner item, never as met; the oasdiff CPA stage proven to fire through the real CPA run of T318a (rev 30, round-29 review M1); every client drift mismatch registered as a finding; the can-i-deploy matrix verdict produced in the CENTRAL C8(ii) pre-release form, with its real post-release re-run named as the post-release step of the WP-41 checkpoint (rev 35, round-34 review B1); HC-4 held for compatibility-window changes.

**Phase-group conventions (P4-P5)**:

- **Paths**: `$SPEC` = `$FEAT` = `specs/001-full-project-audit-remediation`; `$EV` = `$SPEC/evidence`; `$AUD` = `$SPEC/audit`. Every `[REVIEW]` verdict is written to `$EV/reviews/<WP>[-<item>][-r<n>].json` (one folder for the whole task list; `-r<n>` is a later review iteration, review verdict row of the abbreviation table), and the merge-review file of a merge commit that CPA itself makes is `$EV/reviews/CPA-merge-<run_id>.json`, its name written by CPA into that commit's `Awaits-Review:` line (T040, T042; Diverged repository bullet); human-checkpoint records go to `$EV/hc/HC-<n>[-<USn>].json`. A path marked `(new)` does not exist yet and is a deliverable of the task that names it (or of the task named in the mark); generated evidence files under `$EV/` and `$AUD/` are all new and are not marked one by one, and paths created by P0-P3 tasks (for example `scripts/commit-push-all.sh`, `tools/evidence/*`, `scripts/build/verify_artifact.sh`, `scripts/register/gate.sh`, `scripts/qa/run_profile.sh`, `$SPEC/matrix/applicability.yaml`, `docs/DOC_SCOPE.yaml`) are not marked here. A new path under a directory that `.gitignore` ignores today (`tools/`, `build/`, `coverage/`) depends on the WP-09 `.gitignore` negation task of P0; paths that no negation covers (`reports/`, `qa-results/`, any `coverage/` directory below the root) are not used here. Top-level `$EV` entries first written in P4-P7 (all listed in the docs/06 §11 layout), each written only by the tasks named: `exceptions/` (T440; T582 only reads it), `flake_ledger.jsonl` (T563), `p5-exit.json` (T457), `p6-exit.json` (T557), `pack/` (T588, T589), `qa/` (T462, T463, T474; also P2 WP-24), `register/` (T576; also P2 WP-20), `release_digests/` (T448), `reproducibility/` (T443), `retest/` (T567, T570), `sbom/` (T445), `verify/` (T581, T582), `wp73/` (T580b, the evidence of the final constitution update). No `$EV` or `$AUD` path is written by the commit-push script (next bullets).
- **Identifiers**: `CT-n` is contract n of the docs/01 §14 inventory (written `Cn` there); `BC-n` is backend candidate n of the docs/07 candidate table (also written `Cn` there). The doc12 conversion classes C1..C6 keep their doc12 names.
- **Containerized runner (TIC)**: `scripts/test-in-container.sh <app> <lane> -- <cmd>` (created in WP-12 (T121), a dispatcher over the T120 wrappers `scripts/containers/run_go.sh`, `run_node.sh`, `run_docs.sh`, `run_scan.sh`, `run_playwright.sh`, the T200a wrappers `run_rust.sh` and `run_kcov.sh`, plus `scripts/containers/run_qa.sh` for the rows of the `qa` app, which run in IMG-QA, the WP-24 QA image of T211 (helixqa, Tesseract, ffmpeg, Playwright browsers); `run_qa.sh` and the `qa` rows of `scripts/containers/lanes.tsv` are delivered by T212, on which every `TIC qa` call depends, named in each such task together with T211; lanes `unit`, `contract`, `integration`, `e2e`, `api`, `docs`, `tooling` and `rust` (the `rust` lane and the app keys `catalogizer-api-client`, `catalogizer-desktop`, `installer-wizard`, `build-scripts` and one per TypeScript submodule added by T200a, on which every TIC call with them depends); digest-pinned images from `build/containers/images.lock.yaml`). The rows of the `tooling` app (`TIC tooling <lane>`, called by T309 to T312, T319, T324, T420, T435a, T453, T510, T514, T553, T554, T570 and T584) run in IMG-TESTUTIL through `run_testutil.sh`, the wrapper the WP-12 lane table names for that app key (abbreviation table); that image must carry python3, pytest, PyYAML, jsonschema, bash, git and jq, proven by a smoke run of `python3 -c 'import pytest, yaml, jsonschema'` and `jq --version` inside it, and a `TIC tooling` RED counts only after that smoke has passed in the same image (a RED caused by a missing interpreter or module is a RED for the wrong reason, §11.4.224(A)); the WP-60 converter tests use `TIC qa tooling` in IMG-QA instead (T460). The rows of the `docs` app (`TIC docs docs`, T520, T542, T545, T546 and T547; the Python validator of T533 runs in the same image) run in IMG-DOCS through `run_docs.sh`, which therefore needs python3 and pytest besides its render tools (docs/16 §6.1 lists them in the IMG-DOCS row), under the same smoke-before-RED rule. Every build of a deliverable artifact (Go binary, web image, Rust bundle, Android APK), and every compile-class lane (mutation runs in IMG-MUT and compiling benchmark lanes included), is submitted to its build container on the remote build host through `scripts/build/dispatch.sh` (T005b; host and component data in `build/hosts.env` and `build/components.json`, driver `cmd/distributed-build`) and resumed by its registered callback (T121a contract), its RED and GREEN evidence taken from the callback records, and returns the artifact with a sha256 manifest checked by `scripts/build/verify_artifact.sh`; no compile-class lane runs locally (T121b); when no qualified build host is reachable, or the dispatch fails for another closed reason, the build is `blocked-unavailable` with that reason (the closed T005b reasons: `host_unreachable`, `no_qualified_host`, `build_liveness_lost`, `build_progress_flat`, `build_wallclock_exceeded`, `driver_secret_lost`, `artifact_unavailable`, and `signing_key_not_provisioned` for a provenance-signing step; apart from these, and never `blocked-unavailable`: `snapshot_mismatch` is detected on the build host and recorded `infra_failed` (T005b), `submodule_uninitialised` and `undeclared_dirty_input` are caller defects that CPA refuses with exit 20, as are `closure_incomplete` (an input closure missing a file the build reads) and `remote_moved_while_suspended` (a remote that moved while a run was suspended), and a CPA remote S3 check that cannot run is `remote_check_unavailable`, exit 20, distinct from a failing check, exit 10), never moved to the bare host or run locally, and only the host identity itself stays the owner input ODG-07; hosts are read only through `build/hosts.env` (T137a, T137). A lane that needs the WP-13 stack (the WP-41 contract tests, the WP-50 to WP-52 fix verification, the T567 retests) is a split lane of T121a: its test binaries are compiled on the remote build host and only the digest-verified binaries are run locally against the stack, its RED and GREEN x3 taken from the callback records, three iterations being three builds (T089a). Every remote build or compile-class lane ships its source as the T005b snapshot manifest: `(path, tree id)` for the root repository and every initialised submodule at every depth, its digest the sha256 of that manifest, which the build host recomputes from what it received (a difference refused as `snapshot_mismatch`), never `git archive <commit>` of the root alone, which omits submodule code; this covers T380, T396, T443, T566, the IMG-MUT mutation runs and the WP-55 module gates and tests that compile submodule code (T436 to T440, T440a). No build or test runs on the bare host (§11.4.173, FR-021).
- **Remote groups, input closure, split lanes and image classes (head rev 17; T005a, T005b, T089a, T121a, T121b, T212)**: (a) a task of P4-P7 that takes GREEN x3 or several remote checks submits them as one build group (`dispatch.sh submit --group <group_id>` per member, closed by `dispatch.sh group-seal <group_id>`), each member's callback a record-only no-op, and continues from the one group callback; a caller reads a group's outcome by its group kind, decided by precedence (`test_failed` or `build_failed` first, then `blocked-unavailable`, `cancelled` or `infra_failed`, then `completed`; the first triggering member within a level, T005b, T121b), members `cancelled_by_group` being neither failures nor triggers, and a group whose kind is a failure is never a partial pass (an unavailable remote check giving `remote_check_unavailable`); only CPA check groups are submitted with `--cancel-on-fail`, never a group of GREEN x3, flake or stress runs (T563, T567 to T569 and their reruns), whose every member runs to its end; every CPA caller or agent waiting for a remote result waits on the notify stream `.audit/builds/notify/events.jsonl` (blocking inotify, never a poll), with `ready_to_resume`, `resume_expired` and `resume_ttl` as T121b defines them; a remote lane that applies a recorded patch follows the P2-P3 audit-patch convention (the patch carried in the shipped snapshot, applied to a copy inside the container, its sha256 in the argv digest); this covers the T443 double build, the T566 candidate builds and checks, the T567 retests and T569 release-seam checks, the mutation runs of WP-61 (T479 to T481, T504a, T561a) and the remote S3 checks of the CPA runs of T442, T581 and T595a; (b) a remote build or compile-class lane (T380, T396, T443, T566, the IMG-MUT mutation runs, the WP-55 module gates and tests) ships only its input closure into the content-addressed tree cache of the build host (T005a, T005b), never a whole snapshot, the snapshot-manifest digest still recomputed remotely; (c) a CPA run that was suspended with exit 16 and is resumed re-runs S1 before S4, which its caller treats as normal (a remote move found by that S1 is integrated by the same rules as in any run); (d) Playwright and QA runs against the stack are split lanes (every one of P4-P7, none run whole on one side): their remote half builds a manifest-verified prebuilt bundle and a runtime-class web image that is brought back and digest-verified, and the IMG-PW or IMG-QA run half executes locally over them; this covers T468, T487, T488, T509, the `qa api` and `qa e2e` profiles of T567 and every Playwright or QA run against the local stack in WP-41, WP-52, WP-60 and WP-61; a P4-P7 task that adds a `split` row to `scripts/containers/lanes.tsv` states the row's `run_image` and `artifact_kind` (T121a: a row without either is refused `run_image_missing` or `artifact_kind_missing`), and a `run_image` of a `compile` class needs a reviewed run-half row of `scripts/containers/local_allowlist.tsv` in the same change set (else `run_half_not_allowlisted`); the tasks named above use the existing rows of T121a and T212 and add none (rev 26, cross-slice request of the P1-P2 slice); (e) every image that a P4-P7 task adds to `build/containers/images.lock.yaml` carries its `class` field there (scanner, analyser, QA, service, runtime, runtime-base or the compile classes), otherwise RUNP refuses it with `class_unknown`: the IMG-MUT tool images (go-mutesting, Stryker, PIT, cargo-mutants; T479 to T481), the contract-test tool images (oasdiff, pact verifiers, Schemathesis; T317, T323), the sonar-scanner image and the ZAP image of the DAST re-check (T357), each added with its class in the change set that adds it; `build/containers/images.lock.yaml` is class G-GATE in the path-class table of T042, so that change set holds the lock edit on a G-GATE verdict and never commits it unheld (20, `path_gate_unheld`): `$EV/reviews/WP-40-gate.json` for T317 (T322a), `$EV/reviews/WP-41-gate.json` for T323 and T332 (T336a), `$EV/reviews/WP-50-T357-gate.json` for T357 (written by T359) and `$EV/reviews/WP-61-gate.json` for T479 to T481 (written by T505), each a verdict whose gate list includes G-GATE; these named files stay valid but are never required: a work package's own verdict whose gate list includes `G-GATE` beside its own gate may hold the lock edit as well (contracts revision 16, T042); the P5 verdicts `$EV/reviews/WP-52-<item>.json`, `$EV/reviews/WP-56.json`, `$EV/reviews/WP-58-<finding id>.json` and `$EV/reviews/WP-57-reeval-<trigger run id>.json` hold the gated paths their changes edit the same way, each with `G-GATE` in its gate list when it does; (f) a `TIC qa tooling` call of P4-P7 (T460, T461, T462, T462a, T463, T472, T474) runs a command only when that command is a reviewed row of `scripts/containers/local_allowlist.tsv`, added by T212, the owner of the allow-list rows for the QA tooling commands later tasks call, or, for a command T212 did not list, by the calling task in its own change set, held on its work package's verdict whose gate list includes G-GATE (the table is a `cpa_code` path, T121b); any other command is refused with 20 `compile_class_local`.
- **Document renders**: every HTML, PDF or DOCX render or export of P4-P7 (the T535 export pipeline, the T536 export wave, the WP-63 D-programme exports, the diagram renders of T534 and the sibling formats of the completion report and the evidence pack of WP-74) runs in the remote `docs render` lane of IMG-DOCS (the render lane of T121; T121a, T176), and every register export of P4-P7 (T574, T577 and the exports regenerated by the register-writes rule) uses `scripts/register/export.sh --render` (T175a), through the T175a staging-and-install path: the callback re-checks the database fingerprint (refusing with `export_db_moved`, nothing written, a fresh export owed, when the database changed meanwhile) and only stages the brought-back siblings in an ignored directory, and `scripts/register/locked.sh -- scripts/register/export.sh --install <build_id>` at a commit window installs them into `docs/register/`, never a callback writing there directly; its outputs brought back and verified before they are written to their tracked paths by the host step of the generated-files rule; Markdown and CSV generation, the SVG text that `scripts/docs/badges.py` writes (a generator, not a render) and every documentation check (links, metadata, scope, export-sync comparison, the `badges` stage, which compares only the README block, and the diagram validator of T533, which reads the raster outputs that the remote lane brought back) stay local in IMG-DOCS.
- **Released helper or option**: a reviewed helper or CPA option (the T435a and T435c pending-row helper, the T442a `--accepted-pins` option) is available to a task only after its release: its review GO committed in the main repository's HEAD, its commit held by every reachable remote tip of `main`, and that GO approved by the owner in `cpa-host`, so the approved snapshot of a CPA run contains it (T042 rev 32; the approval recorded in `$EV/hc/owner-trust/<n>.json`, T046a), cited by the CPA run record of the run that pushed it and by that approval record; CPA code never runs on the GO and the push alone, only once the owner has approved that GO; an edge "after the release of T435b" or "after the release of T442b" means exactly that. The approval (rev 34, round-33 review M3, I4, M1; rev 35, round-34 review I1): the conductor only names the GO introduction commit (the commit that introduced the GO verdict file) and the owner runs `cpa-host --owner-trust approve <verdict> --commit <that commit>`, which refuses `approval_not_gate_go` (not a G-GATE GO, or `blocking_findings` above 0), `reviewed_files_incomplete` (a G-GATE path changed by a commit of `covers_runs` missing from the verdict's `reviewed_files`, or a path named by the `scripts/repo/cpa_code.txt` at the approval source, the `--commit`, that is neither in the approved manifest nor in that list), `review_provenance_invalid` (the approved checker refuses the verdict at `--commit`), `reviewed_files_foreign_change` (a listed path changed since its approved entry by a main-repository commit that is neither in this verdict's `covers_runs` nor under an already owner-approved GO) and `approval_older_than_manifest` (a listed path's source commit is an ancestor of the commit behind its current approved entry, unless `--recovery`) (CENTRAL C6; a GO superseded by a later owed GO that lists newer content of each of its paths is closed `superseded` and need not be approved, CENTRAL C7), so every G-GATE verdict of P3-P7 lists in `reviewed_files` each G-GATE path held on it with its sha256, and a `commit_push.conf` key that CPA code reads is listed on the same verdict as that code; an approval after the adoption runs the approved checker from the store through `cpa-host --check-provenance <verdict>`, never the working-tree checker (CENTRAL C5; T046a); an approval is owed for a GO whose reviewed files intersect the CPA-executed set (the union of the approved and the HEAD `scripts/repo/cpa_code.txt` and the paths they list, the CPA tables `scripts/release/release_seam_files.txt`, `scripts/qa/guard_registry.tsv`, `scripts/repo/validate_checks.tsv` and `scripts/repo/path_gates.tsv`, the schema, `commit_push.conf` and every path the approved or the HEAD `scripts/release/release_seam_files.txt` names, scripts and data files, a release-seam GO being owed like any other), every other GO being listed, not owed (CENTRAL C7). A direct call, outside a CPA run, of a released G-GATE helper with the CPA lock held (`scripts/repo/record_pending_pin.sh --ff`, `--rollback`, `--advance-third-party` and `--settle-nested` without `--in-hold`, as T436 to T439, T579a and T580b call it), and of every release-seam script (such as `scripts/perf/release_check.sh` and `scripts/release/qa_handoff_gate.sh`), runs only through `cpa-host --exec-approved <path> [args...]`, which executes the approved export of that path, never the working-tree file (CENTRAL C8); `cpa-host` refuses with 20 a path that the approved manifest does not hold, as `release_seam_unreleased` for a release-seam path and as `helper_not_approved` for any other helper; no helper compares its own sha256 with the manifest as a control (a self-check is bypassable; it stays at most an accidental-drift note); fixture in the test of each script that makes such a call, on the T039 harness: a helper path that the test-state manifest does not hold, called through `--exec-approved`, is refused with the code of its path class (`release_seam_unreleased` for a release-seam path, `helper_not_approved` for any other helper; each caller's fixture names the one its path's class gives, CENTRAL C8) and changes nothing, and with a working-tree copy that differs by one byte from its manifest entry and writes a marker file, the call runs the approved export and no marker is written; paired mutation: a caller that execs the working-tree path writes the marker and the fixture FAILs; a call of a working-tree helper path outside `--exec-approved` found in review is a blocking finding, except a call by the script's own unit-test file (as the T324 test calls `scripts/contract/can_i_deploy.sh` with `--root` on its fixtures; CENTRAL C8); a producing task whose release-seam script or helper is not yet approved uses the pre-release production form of CENTRAL C8(ii) (T335), whose output is marked `pre_release` and is never accepted by T569, T580, T580a, T582 or T564a.
- **Evidence**: every run goes through `tools/evidence/evrec` into `$EV/ledger.jsonl` as an `ev/1` record (`$SPEC/contracts/evidence-record.schema.json`); item verdicts are derived by `tools/evidence/verdict` into `$EV/verdicts/<ATM-id>.json`, never written by hand (review verdicts never go there).
- **Commit-push outputs and clean-tree checks** (abbreviation table: `$CPA_RUN`, CPA run record, clean tracked tree): the commit-push script (CPA, WP-04, T042) writes nothing into the tracked tree and commits none of its own outputs: its `report.json`, `summary.txt`, S7 verifier JSON `verify.json`, stage transcripts, deferral rows, the §9.2 backup of a merge integration under `backup/` (a `git bundle` of the local range checked by `git bundle verify`, plus a copy of every uncommitted file under `backup/worktree/` with its sha256) and the conflicting files of a refused merge under `conflicts/` stay in its ignored run directory `$CPA_RUN` = `.audit/commit-push/<run_id>/` (never tmpfs; `<run_id>` = UTC time, process id and a random suffix); besides that directory a run that holds the lock writes only two other ignored places, its lock and long-op registry records under `.audit/longops/` (T089) and the pending-pin rows of `.audit/pending_pins.tsv` (T042a), and a run that does not get the lock writes only its own run directory and touches nothing else. Git itself is the tracked record of a push: every commit CPA makes carries the trailer `CPA-Run: <run_id>` and, in its message body, its deferral flags (`Deferred-Gates:` with `SKIP_LONG`, `SWEEP_ABSENT` or `LOCAL_ONLY`), on a held commit `Awaits-Review: <verdict path>`, and `Foreign-Commit: <sha>` lines naming the commits that S1 brought in from a live remote tip and that are not CPA commits (the T042 S0 predicate, round-25 review B1: a commit carrying `CPA-Run: <id>` is a CPA commit only when this clone's `.audit/commit-push/<id>/commits.tsv` lists its repository path, sha and run id, or a committed GO lists them in `covers_runs`; a copied or forged trailer counts as none; only commits reachable from a live remote tip at S1 are ever named; a local commit that is no CPA commit and that no remote holds, such as a plain `git commit` outside CPA or a hand commit with a copied trailer, is refused with 20 `unrecorded_local_commit` and never named, T042). A task that needs a run's report or verifier result as evidence cites the CPA run record: after the run it captures `$CPA_RUN/report.json` (and `verify.json` where needed) with `tools/evidence/evrec`, an `ev/1` entry whose blob `$EV/blobs/<sha256>` is the file byte for byte, and that entry and blob are ordinary members of the task's next declared change set. Shared stores (`$EV/ledger.jsonl`, `$EV/blobs/`) belong to the change set of whichever task wrote to them; a CPA run refuses only untracked or modified files outside its declared change set (T042). Every clean-tree or `dirty` condition of P4-P7 (T429, T442, T579a, T582, T595b) is measured on the clean tracked tree of the abbreviation table: `scripts/repo/verify_repos.sh --no-remote` reports `summary.dirty` equal to `summary.dirty_excepted`, each repository judged by `git status --porcelain --ignore-submodules=all` (untracked files counted, ignored paths such as `.audit/` never), excepted rows coming only from the reviewed `scripts/repo/exceptions.tsv` (T032; the docling `dirty` row, permanently modified CRLF test data, is such a row), pin drift reported beside it and matched against `.audit/pending_pins.tsv`; no test or gate of P4-P7 asserts a raw `git status --porcelain` on the main repository, which also prints a dirty or moved submodule; and the measurement cites, by its report sha256, the CPA run record of the run that made the measured HEAD (its run id read from the `CPA-Run:` trailer of that commit), or records `report_sha256: null` with a reason when HEAD is not a CPA commit or that report is absent on this host (clean tracked tree row of the abbreviation table).
- **Generated tracked files**: the container-outputs rule of the P0-P1 conventions applies (a containerized step writes only to `/out`, RUNP `--out <dir>`, default the ignored `.audit/out/<op_id>/`; no container writes `/src` except `scripts/register/locked.sh` through `RUNP --rw docs`, T064). In P4-P7 every tracked file a containerized step generates or edits (a route baseline or dump, a drift or contract report, a converted bank file, a regenerated bank-id floor, a wave assignment, a dependency report, a schema dump, an index, a diagram render, an export twin, a badge or a generated reference; for example T312, T314, T319, T453, T454, T462, T463 to T472, T523, T534 to T537, T541, T542 and T545) is written under `/out` at its repository-relative path, and a host step of the same task, after the container has exited, copies each such file to that path and records the `/out` source and the tracked destination with their sha256, which must be equal, in the task's `ev/1` entry; a test that asserts a generated file asserts it under `/out` (or under the output variable that points there). The copy is a file operation, not a build or a test, so it does not breach the no-bare-host rule.
- **Commit windows (parallel streams)**: the P0-P1 commit-window rule applies (§11.4.84): the working tree is shared by every stream and CPA refuses an uncommitted file its declared change set does not name, so at a window every stream stops writing, releases its long-op registrations and hands the conductor (ST-GOV) its uncommitted paths, each with the review verdict it still waits for, and the conductor runs one CPA run over their union as `--paths-from` (T042); T580e (rev 28) is the one exception: its main-repository runs are held commits on distinct verdict files, so each run folds the uncommitted WP-73 records into its own `--paths-from` list and the conductor grants the main-repository commit turn to one run at a time through `scripts/release/commit_turn_check.sh` (`commit_turn_conflict`, T580e); no separate records-only window run precedes them; ordering (rev 29, T580e): a general window commits every record that is not a WP-73 record of the T580e (0) list before a turn is granted, no general window starts while a turn is granted, and from the grant until that run commits or is refused at S0 no other stream writes the main working tree (`evrec` refuses `commit_turn_held`, T050; ST-REV writes its T580f and T580a verdict files after the release); the freeze applies to writers other than the granted run: the granted run's own `evrec` writes, made with `EVREC_TURN_RUN_ID` equal to the run id of the grant, are allowed, including those of its `CPA --resume`, and a granted run that exits 16 `awaiting_remote_checks` keeps its grant, and the freeze, until its resume commits or is refused at S0 or the grant is released by the conductor with `--release`, or reaped by `--reap` once its holder is proven dead (never by age); a grant has no time-based expiry, and every release and reap is recorded as an `ev/1` entry (rev 30, round-29 review; the matching-`EVREC_TURN_RUN_ID` exemption is T050's, with its T049 fixture and T056 mutation, the grant lifetime T580e's, fixture (xiv)); CPA bootstrap is the owner install checkpoint T046a; recovery from a defective CPA release is the owner recovery of CENTRAL C11 (the reviewed fixing GO approved uncommitted from the working tree with `--recovery`, its files then declared unheld by the next run); there is no self-release mode and no CPA waiver, and no separate rule of this task list; a CPA run that ends with exit code 16 `awaiting_remote_checks` (its S3 checks suspended on the remote build host, T121b) has committed nothing, and a resumed run that suspends again (16 again) is still open: the group callback only re-arms the run (`ready_to_resume`), and the resume run is made by the conductor with `CPA --resume`, never by the hub; the window stays open, the run is resumed when its checks report, and no task counts it as committed or pushed (this holds for every CPA caller of P4-P7: the commit windows, the G-PIN pointer runs of T442, the WP-73 runs of T580b and T581, and T595a); a stream never declares another stream's files to get past a refusal, and a `--repo <path>` run, whose S0 sweep is scoped to `<path>` (T042a), is not stopped by another stream's uncommitted files elsewhere. A file that open tasks of two streams edit is held by one stream at a time, because a window commits a path on one verdict only, so one stream's change to it would otherwise ride on the other stream's review: the rule applies to any file that open tasks of two streams edit, for example the compose files (`docker-compose.yml`, `deployment/docker-compose.yml`, `docker-compose.test.yml`; T351 ST-SEC, T376 ST-API, T448 ST-INFRA and T456a ST-GOV, in a fixed order: T448, which depends on T351 and T376, converts them only after their change sets are pushed, and T456a edits them only after the T448 commit is pushed) and the client files of the T349 change set (ST-WEB, ST-AND); in P4 the G-GATE files `build/containers/images.lock.yaml`, `scripts/repo/validate_checks.tsv` and `scripts/repo/cpa_code.txt` are edited by ST-API (T317 and T318, held on `$EV/reviews/WP-40-gate.json`) and by ST-QA (T323 and T332, held on `$EV/reviews/WP-41-gate.json`, with the T334a scanner, a file that `cpa_code.txt` lists, and the standing guard registry `scripts/qa/guard_registry.tsv`, a G-GATE row of `scripts/repo/path_gates.tsv` (T042), created by T334a and given its rows by T327, T328 and T329, on the same verdict), in a fixed order: ST-API holds them first, and ST-QA makes its first edit of any of them only after the T317 and T318 commits are released by the T322a GO; in P5 the main case is `catalog-api/main.go`, edited at least by the WP-50 change sets of T339, T341, T343, T350 and T353 (ST-SEC) and by T368, T376 and, where its envelope change reaches that file, T375 of WP-51 (ST-API); the conductor grants the file to one of the two streams and records the holder in the `ev/1` entry of the window run, and the other stream starts its edit only after the holder's change to the file is committed and released by its review's GO, or undone by the NO-GO procedure (Review before push bullet).
- **Fix protocol (FP)** for every [TDD] fix task in P5 (docs/06 §4, §11.4.115(F)): (1) root-cause note on the register item (`docs/workable_items.db`, FR-008, §11.4.102); (2) RED `ev/1` entry on the pre-fix artifact fingerprint, observed before the fix is written; (3) the fix; (4) GREEN on a different artifact fingerprint, three identical GREEN iterations; (5) reviewer-authored mutation recorded as a caught `MUTATION` entry (§11.4.194(6)(d)); (6) clean-target verification of the built artifact (FR-021, §11.4.200); (7) commit through `scripts/commit-push-all.sh` (CPA) on `main` only, no force-push (FR-024, §11.4.113). Work committed inside a submodule repository (T430, T431, T433, T440 (b) for the L6 nested third-party gitlinks of `submodules/helix_qa`, T440a for a nested third-party gitlink of an own-organisation module and for its manifest and lock-file bumps inside an own-organisation submodule (`CPA --repo <module> --paths-from ... --awaits-review`; T440a never makes a `CPA --repo submodules/constitution` run, its constitution-scope rows being recorded `owed_to_T580b` only, for T580b (3c)), T440c for its push runs (`CPA --repo submodules/helix_qa` and one per owned parent of the L6 module commits), T499, T501, T572 where the strengthened test lives in a submodule, and the commit that T580b (3c) makes inside the constitution repository: the engine gitlinks with the constitution's own work that T430 and T499 owe there) uses the per-repository mode `CPA --repo <path>` of WP-04 (T042a): it commits in, and pushes from, that repository only, to that repository's remotes as enumerated at run time, and leaves every ancestor repository's HEAD and gitlink unchanged; in main mode a declared path below a gitlink, held or not, is refused (20, `path_in_submodule`, T042): main mode never commits inside a submodule, so a pointer change is the `--repo` commit first and then a G-PIN pointer move in the parent, and unreviewed submodule work never rides on a main-repository change set; a gitlink moves only through a pointer commit in the parent that has passed its G-PIN review (docs/11 §6.4 step 7: T441 before the T442 layer commits of WP-55, T580a before the final pointer moves of WP-73 T581 and the constitution update T580b), never as a side effect of a module commit, and a pointer commit never publishes a pin that no remote of that submodule holds (the submodule is pushed first, docs/16 §11.1 R4). Each `--repo` commit records its pending pin move (repository path, new gitlink sha, run id) in the ignored file `.audit/pending_pins.tsv`, and the task that ran that commit run captures its CPA run record with `evrec` (its `report.json` lists the commits made with their run id), so that WP-73 can tell this feature's upstream commits from another actor's from tracked records (WP-73 Inputs); a fast-forward that moves a submodule HEAD without a commit (the WP-55 layer moves of T436 to T439, the late catch-up of T579a and the constitution fast-forward and engine checkouts of T580b) is made together with its row decision in one hold of the CPA lock by the reviewed helper `scripts/repo/record_pending_pin.sh --ff <path> <sha>` (T435a), called only through `cpa-host --exec-approved` (released-helper bullet, CENTRAL C8), which writes or replaces the row when the move left HEAD different from the parent's gitlink and removes it when HEAD equals the gitlink, and a rollback of that move is made with its row decision in one lock hold by the helper's `--rollback <path> <old>` mode, which restores a row for the HEAD the rollback returned to while that HEAD still differs from the parent's gitlink (an earlier `--repo` commit of T430, T431, T499 or T572) and removes the row when HEAD equals the gitlink again (the `--after-rollback` decision); after every move of a repository that holds nested gitlinks (the S1 fast-forward or merge of a `--repo` run, and the helper's `--ff` and `--rollback`; today `submodules/helix_qa`, whose nested gitlinks are all third-party, and `submodules/constitution`) the nested entries of `git -C <repository> diff --raw <old> <new>` are settled in the same lock hold by the helper's `--settle-nested` mode (T435a: the helper's own moves run it before they release the lock, and a CPA run calls it under its own hold after S1 with `--in-hold <run_id>`, T042a), by status: `M` of a third-party path through `--sync-third-party`, `M` of an owned path through `--ff` (or, when a pending row names it, by the row rule of T435a), `A` through `--init` and `D` through `--retire`, which moves the leftover checkout, never deleting it, to the ignored `.audit/removed/<op_id>/<path>/` with its sha256 list; no third-party path gets a row from these settlement modes (the only rows of third-party paths are those of the reviewed `--advance-third-party` mode of T435c, each for an upstream tip that T440 or T440a tested GREEN x3, and the settle mode treats them by its row rule), and every refusal is recorded unsettled (`nested_unsettled`), which stops the calling task (T435a); the ODG-13 basis, decided by the owner's FR-017 answer recorded by T012a (spec FR-017 revision 8: every pin moves to its latest upstream once its tests pass): bringing a nested third-party checkout to the pin that its parent module's own commits record follows that module, so these settlements proceed, T440 reports them as followed parent pins and T440a re-evaluates them against the latest upstream; no `CPA --repo submodules/constitution` run is made before the T580b constitution update, because its S1 would move the constitution to a remote tip that T580b has not reviewed: the work owed in that repository itself (its T430 row, a T499 module test) is made in the T580b (3c) run and reviewed by T580a, and the constitution moves, with its nested engines, only there; a helper call refused because another op holds the lock moves nothing and changes no row, and is re-run, the same command, once the lock is free (each refusal captured in the task's evidence), never replaced by a move made by hand; in P4-P7 that helper is the only writer of rows for moves that are not commits (the integrate-only `--repo` run of T042a is not used for them); a main-repository CPA run reports a pin drift that exactly matches a pending row as pending, not failing, while any other drift still exits 15; the pointer commit of the G-PIN layer (T442, T581, and `CPA --repo <parent>` for a nested parent such as the constitution in T580b) consumes, that is removes, the rows of the pins it moves (T042a); and the S0 sweep of a `--repo` run is scoped to `<path>` (T042a). The same pending rows are what the standalone verifier runs of WP-55 accept as pending (T429, T435, T442).
- **blocked-unavailable**: a test or build needing an absent real service, credential, device or reachable build host records the one status term of this task list, `blocked-unavailable`, with `blocked_reason` naming the exact missing item (for a dispatched build, one of the closed T005b reasons, `driver_secret_lost` and `artifact_unavailable` included; `closure_incomplete` and `remote_moved_while_suspended` are refusals (CPA exit 20), not reasons of this status; `snapshot_mismatch` (recorded `infra_failed`, T005b), `submodule_uninitialised` and `undeclared_dirty_input` (caller defects, CPA exit 20) and `remote_check_unavailable` (CPA exit 20, distinct from a failing check, exit 10) are not `blocked-unavailable` reasons) and `counts_as: not_passing` (FR-025, spec FR-025 revision 8, docs/05 §10); it is never a pass or a skip, and it is distinct from a defect failure.
- **Findings in verdicts**: a review that records findings writes each in the verdict's `findings[]` with `finding_layer` from the contract enum (`source`, `artifact` or `runtime`; contracts revision 11) and the docs/12 class in `finding_class` beside it.
- **Producer is not verifier**: every [REVIEW] task is a pure review owned by ST-REV on Opus at xhigh (§11.4.209, §11.4.240), started through the Workflow `agent()` path (the dispatch path that sets model and effort) and carrying the review provenance record that T094a and T094d check, iterates to zero blocking findings (§11.4.134), writes its verdict to `$EV/reviews/`, and never produces the reviewed work; fixes found by a review go back to the producing stream. Every verdict file has the `review-verdict/1` format of the review verdict row of the abbreviation table, with every field that `$FEAT/contracts/review-verdict.schema.json` requires: `schema` (`review-verdict/1`), `verdict` (`GO` or `NO-GO`), `blocking_findings` (the count of blocking findings, 0 for a GO), `covers_runs` (one entry per commit the review covers: its `CPA-Run` id, which is the key a hold is released on, with its repository path and commit sha, read from the commit trailers; an empty list when no commit awaits the verdict), `model` and `effort` (the model and effort that ran the review); `gate`, `author` and `reviewer` are optional.
- **Review before push**: a change made before the `[REVIEW]` GO that covers it is committed as a held commit: its paths go into the declared change set with that review's verdict file in the second column of the `--paths-from` list (or the whole run is held with `--awaits-review <verdict file>`), so the commit carries `Deferred-Gates: LOCAL_ONLY` and `Awaits-Review: <verdict file>` beside its `CPA-Run` trailer (WP-04 T039, T041, T042; `--repo <path>` runs hold the same way, T042a; in main mode a held path inside a submodule is refused with 20, so submodule work is held through `--repo <path>` and reaches its parent only through a G-PIN pointer move). The verdict path of an `Awaits-Review:` line is always relative to the main-repository root and is always read from the main repository's committed HEAD (`git -C <main root> show HEAD:<path>`), whichever repository holds the commit: a held commit inside a submodule is released by its verdict committed in the main repository, never by a file in the submodule's own tree. S6 of every later CPA run, main-repository and `--repo` alike, pushes a held commit only when that verdict file is committed in the main repository's HEAD with `verdict: GO` and its `covers_runs` lists the held commit's `CPA-Run` id; until then it pushes nothing past the held commit and the run exits 14 with reason `review_pending` naming each held commit and its verdict. So no stream's run publishes another stream's unreviewed commit on the shared `main`, and no task pushes unreviewed work to any remote (§11.4.142, §11.4.125); the owed push is made by the first CPA run after that GO is committed in the main repository (a `--repo` run for a submodule's held commits), or by a later one, and is not a dependency edge of the producing task. A hold on a verdict file that already holds GO in the main repository's HEAD is refused (20, `verdict_already_go`, T042): work made after a GO waits on the verdict file of a new review iteration (`<WP>[-<item>]-r<n>.json`), so an earlier GO never covers later work. A held commit whose review ends in a NO-GO that abandons the change is undone by the NO-GO procedure of the P0-P1 commit-window rule, which governs this bullet: at the next window the producing stream runs `git revert --no-commit <held commits>`, `git revert --quit` and `git restore --staged -- <reverted paths>` (CPA has no revert operation, and a plain `git revert` would make a local commit that is no CPA commit under the T042 S0 predicate, which S1 refuses with 20, `unrecorded_local_commit`), and the conductor commits the reverted paths through CPA, declared and held on the same verdict file (14); when the reverted commits move nested gitlinks (the helix_qa commits of T440 (b) and T440c, a nested module commit of T440a), that revert is committed by `CPA --repo <module> --reverting <held commits>` (T042a), and CPA itself, in its own lock hold right after committing the revert, calls `scripts/repo/record_pending_pin.sh --settle-nested <module> <pre-revert HEAD> <revert commit> --reverting --in-hold <run_id> --out $CPA_RUN/settle/` (T435a; this argument order everywhere; a call from the conductor or any process outside that run is refused with 20): each nested path is returned to the gitlink that the revert restores (a third-party checkout detached there, an owned one fast-forward or back on `main` only to a commit every remote holds) and its pending row is removed, a refusal recorded `nested_unsettled`; the module's own row then names the revert commit (HEAD still differs from the parent's gitlink), which the next pointer commit that moves the module consumes or which stays pending to WP-73 (T580a (b), T581), never a reset, rebase or force-push (§11.4.113); S6 still pushes nothing past the held commit below it; ST-REV then writes GO into that verdict file, its `covers_runs` naming the held commits and the revert commit and stating that the net change pushed is none, which releases both, so the abandoned change is published only together with its reversal (a GO that names the held commits without the revert is refused at S5 before it is committed, 20, `verdict_covers_incomplete`, T039, T042). Review verdict files and human-checkpoint records are gate records, committed and pushed by ordinary runs. In P5 the commit of FP step 7 is pushed only after the review task of its work package returns GO for that change (T359, T360, T378, T379, T395, T398, T411, T428, T432, T434a, T435b, T440b, T441, T442b, T451, T456); in P4 the G-CONTRACT (T322) and WP-41 (T336) reviews and the G-GATE reviews T322a and T336a gate the pushes.
- **Diverged repository** (plan owner's rule (Y); WP-04 T040, T042, T042a): when a remote of a repository moves while that repository holds local commits that no remote has (a held commit awaiting its GO, or a released one not yet pushed), the repository is not left diverged: the next CPA run over it (main-repository or `--repo <path>`), under the CPA lock and after its §9.2 backup under `$CPA_RUN/backup/`, integrates the newest live remote tip itself through `scripts/repo/integrate_merge.sh` (T040) with `git merge --no-ff <live remote tip>`, never a rebase, reset or force-push (§11.4.113); the merge commit carries `CPA-Run:` and one `Foreign-Commit: <sha>` line per incoming remote commit that is no CPA commit (T042 S0 predicate: a forged or copied trailer counts as none, so a foreign commit of another clone that no committed GO lists is named), and in a submodule replaces that repository's pending pin row (T042a). Whenever it merges into a held range (a commit below it carries an `Awaits-Review:` line and is not yet on every remote, whether or not its verdict already holds GO) or resolves conflicts (a merge with a conflict is refused with 12, `merge_conflict`, nothing moved and the conflicting files copied under `$CPA_RUN/conflicts/`; it is made only by a later `--resolve-merge <dir>` run whose resolution, written under `.audit/merge-resolution/<run_id>/` of the refused run (any other directory gives 20, `resolution_dir_invalid`), was made on Opus at xhigh, §11.4.211, T040, T042), it is held on its own merge-review file `$EV/reviews/CPA-merge-<run_id>.json`, which CPA itself writes into its `Awaits-Review:` line (T040, T042), never on the verdict file the held range awaits and never on an `-r<n>` iteration of it. S6 pushes nothing below an unreleased CPA merge commit (T041), and the range is pushed only once both kinds of verdict are GO: each held commit's own verdict, and the merge-review file, which the reviewer of the range the merge went into writes after reviewing the merge commit with its incoming range (only the remote's commits brought in, every held change kept), its `covers_runs` naming the merge run: T432 for the module change sets of T430 and T431 (pushed by T433), T500 for those of T499 (T501), T441 (layer L6) for the `submodules/helix_qa` commit of T440 (b) (pushed by T440c), T440b for the nested module commits of T440a (pushed by T440a before T442 L6, else by T581 step (1)), the covering T571 re-draw for the T572 commits in a submodule, T580a for every repository other than the main repository that WP-73 pushes (the constitution included: T580b, T581 (1) and (2)), and the standing merge review T308a for every merge in the main repository (the commit windows of P4 to P7, the G-PIN pointer runs of T442, the WP-73 root runs of T581 and the closing push T595a). That GO is committed in the main repository's HEAD before the run that pushes is re-run: for a merge inside a submodule by a main-repository CPA run made first, for a main-repository merge by an earlier window or by the re-run's own declared change set (T039). A merge made by hand is no CPA commit (no run record and no committed GO lists it, whatever trailer it carries) and no remote holds it, so it stays refused with 20 (`unrecorded_local_commit`, T040), a merge left in progress (`MERGE_HEAD` present) is refused at S0 with 20 (`merge_in_progress`; one that a killed CPA run left is attributed through its merge record `merge.json` and named with its remediation, T040, T042, T090), while a merge that a live CPA run is still making is met as that run's lock: a second run started meanwhile is refused with 20 `lock_held` (T039), never `merge_in_progress`; and no P4-P7 task merges outside CPA. Every gitlink-moving commit of P4-P7 (T440 (b), T440c, T440a nested commits, T580b (3c), T581, T595a) is made by a run that passes `--accepted-pins` or stages the gitlink path held on any verdict at S2, G-PIN in the gate list and the accepted sha being checked at S5 on the GO that releases it (`verdict_gate_mismatch`, `verdict_pins_incomplete`, T042), and a main-mode run never commits inside a submodule (`path_in_submodule`); in main mode S6 judges the net gitlink change of the outgoing range per remote tip, a gitlink whose new sha a reachable remote tip of `main` already holds being exempt, and refuses with 20 a net change that no accepting G-PIN verdict covers (`outgoing_gitlink_not_accepted`, T042); there is no per-commit check, and a nested pointer commit made with `CPA --repo <parent>` (T440 (b), T440c's merge, T440a nested commits, T580b (3c)) likewise passes `--accepted-pins` or stages the gitlink path held on any verdict at S2, and the GO that releases it has a gate list that includes G-PIN (else S5 refuses with 20, `verdict_gate_mismatch`, T042) with `accepted_pins` matching the moved shas (paths from the main repository root; a deleted submodule's entry with sha `null`, contracts revision 14), else S5 refuses with 20 (`verdict_pins_incomplete`, T042). Every GO of this task list, a merge-review file's included, lists in `covers_runs` every held commit that awaits its file, or the run that commits it is refused with 20 (`verdict_covers_incomplete`, T042). The held module commits of T430, T431, T499 and T572 and the constitution commit of T580b integrate this way when their upstream moves while they wait (T433, T501, T572, T580b, T581); inside WP-73 each repository gets at most one such merge-and-review round, and a further move of its remote is an ODG-41 row (WP-73 Inputs), never a further round. A foreign push that changes a path which the declared change set of a window also changes stops that run with 12 (`ff_blocked_by_local_changes`, nothing moved); the window is then re-run in the commit-before-integrate mode of T040 and T042: under the CPA lock and after its §9.2 bundle backup, CPA first commits the declared change set as ordinary CPA commits (held where declared) and then runs the merge path, so the overlap gives either a clean merge or a `merge_conflict` that a `--resolve-merge` run settles, and either merge is reviewed like any other (in the main repository by the standing merge review T308a). The hash-chained `$EV/ledger.jsonl` and the binary `docs/workable_items.db` each have one writer (`tools/evidence/evrec`; ST-REG through `scripts/register/locked.sh` and the T066 procedure), and a conflict in either is never merged as text: the remote side is kept and the local entries or rows are recorded again on top of it by that writer (T040, T042); a re-recorded ledger entry gets a new `seq`, and the `--resolve-merge` resolution holds only the conflicting files (T040), so a `ledger#<seq>` reference to it in any other file of the merged tree still names the old `seq`: the reviewer of the merge (in the main repository, where the ledger lives, the standing merge review T308a) derives the old and new `seq` of each re-recorded entry from the backup bundle and the merged ledger (the same entry body at a new `seq`), checks every `ledger#<seq>` reference of the merged tree against that list and with `tools/evidence/verify`, and returns NO-GO on a reference that still names an old `seq`; the repair, the reference rewritten by the stream that owns the citing file in a declared change set above the merge, is reviewed again there before the range is released; the remediation of every code-12 reason is the one `docs/scripts/commit-push-all.md` gives (T045).
- **Register writes**: every mutating `$WI` or `sqlite3` command on `docs/workable_items.db` runs through `scripts/register/locked.sh -- <cmd>` (T064), which holds `flock docs/.register.lock` around exactly one command (single writer, doc04 §12.2; a bare mutating call is a review finding), in IMG-TESTUTIL (the image T008 maps to `sqlite3`); read-only queries use the `immutable=1` URI (T071) under the read precondition of the P0-P1 conventions: a read is either one `locked.sh` call that runs `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` and then the query, or a reader that refuses (20) while `docs/workable_items.db-wal` is non-empty, because an `immutable=1` reader does not see rows still in the WAL (docs/04 §12.2; 2 rows where a `mode=ro` reader saw 3); the T066 dump-and-commit procedure ends every committed write with that checkpoint, and a read-only step of a clean-tree or release seam (the release-seam checks of T569 and T582) is always a refusing reader, never a checkpointing one, because a checkpoint of uncommitted rows would rewrite the tracked database; a bulk write first takes the SQLite pre-op backup of the P0-P1 register rule (§9.2) through the reviewed helper `scripts/register/backup_db.sh --record <file>` (T064a): the online `.backup` (or `VACUUM INTO`) under the register lock to the ignored `docs/workable_items.db.bak-<UTC>` (covered by `docs/*.bak-*`, never an untracked file in the tracked tree), `PRAGMA integrity_check` = ok on the backup and its restore probe (the backup restored into a scratch database whose canonical dump must equal the source dump taken under the lock), both sha256 values, both row counts and the image digest recorded, and a non-zero exit, never a reported backup, when a check fails; never a hardlinked `cp -al` copy, whose hardlink shares the page file that SQLite rewrites in place, so it changes with the live database and protects nothing; then `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`, `scripts/register/gate.sh` and the T066 dump-and-commit procedure (DB, `docs/register/register.sql` and the documents regenerated by `scripts/register/export.sh` and `scripts/register/reconcile.sh` of T067, committed together); the large-file bound of class `generated` in the reviewed path-class table (plan owner's rules (Z) and (V); T040b; Path classes bullet) holds for every P4-P7 write up to the T576 closure sweep: 16 MiB (16,777,216 B) per file, the one register bound of this plan, for `docs/workable_items.db` and for every file under `docs/register/**` (the dump `docs/register/register.sql`, the reconciliation outputs and the regenerated exports with their HTML, PDF and DOCX siblings; T574, T577), derived with both stored copies of every description (`items.description` and `body_md`) and the measured `docs/issues` length distribution (T040b, T067); every item description a P4-P7 task writes follows the bounded description policy of T168 (at most 2,048 bytes, its Sources block included, the full ticket text staying in the source file that the Sources block cites by path and sha256), and a write that would still cross the bound stops for the held reviewed table change of T040b (a G-DATA review iteration `$EV/reviews/WP-06-r<n>.json` carrying the measured sizes), the database, the dump and every regenerated export that the raise admits declared held on that same iteration together with the raise (T040b: a path not held on the table change's own verdict is judged with the HEAD tables, and one whose result the new tables would change is refused with 20, `table_admits_unheld_path`; T178), never committed past the check. Findings are written as one `finding/1` file per finding under `$AUD/findings/` and linked to their register item through ST-REG.
- **Inherited P0-P3 rules** (abbreviation table and P0-P1 conventions, unchanged here): (a) disk headroom: every local `podman build`, `podman pull` and container run of P4-P7 (every `RUNP` and `TIC` call through the precondition built into `RUNP`, and every direct pull of a pinned tool image, for example in T317, T445 and T543) first runs `scripts/containers/disk_headroom.sh --op <op_id>` (T001), is refused with `disk_below_headroom` below the threshold and records its before and after values in `$EV/disk/<op_id>.json` (T582 alone sets `DISK_HEADROOM_OUT_DIR=.audit/out/<op_id>/disk/`, T001, so that nothing reaches the tracked tree before its strict run); images built here carry `--label project=catalogizer` and cleanup removes only labelled images and containers, never a global prune; (b) every task that writes a `docs/scripts/*.md` companion (§11.4.18) adds its row to the index `docs/scripts/README.md` (T036) in the same change, and a companion written beside its script (for example `scripts/contract/README.md`, T309) gets an index row pointing to it; (c) the ratchet baselines `scripts/repo/validate_baselines/<check>.tsv` (T040), measured over the main repository and every own-organisation repository at every depth with every key taken from the main root (plan owner's rule (W), as the secrets baseline of T040a), so that a `--repo` run of P5 scores the rows under its path and a violation that already existed in a module is a counted row, never a new key, only shrink: a task that removes counted violations lowers or deletes their rows in the same change (T448 for the main-repository rows of `check_pins.tsv`, T472 and T474 for `qa_banks.tsv` and the `challenges/helixqa-banks/` rows of the anti-bluff baseline), and no task raises a count; the rows of each own-organisation submodule repository form that repository's items (T092 registers one item per `(check, rule, repository)` group; T105), fixed or closed on a stated allowed basis by its module work (T430, T499), never lowered by another work package's main-repository task; because a `--repo` change set cannot declare the main-repository baseline file (`path_outside_repo`, T042a), a `--repo` run in which a declared file's count falls below its row is not refused: the run reports that row `baseline_lowering_owed` (key, row, new count, run id) in its report, never exit 10 and never silently (T040, T042a), and the task that ran it captures that report with its CPA run record (FP step 7); the lowering is that module work's own change, made in the main-repository change set of the pointer commit that moves that module's pin past the commit (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> <new pin>`): T442 for a WP-55 layer, T581 for every pin that WP-73 moves (the constitution's pin carrying the rows of its nested engines' fixes); that change set lowers every row whose count at the new pin is below the row in the files the move brings in (`git diff --name-only <old pin> <new pin>` in the moved repository, nested gitlinks followed, keyed from the main root, which T040 holds to the lowering rule as declared files): the rows those reports name and the rows that `baseline_drift` records as lowered (a count that another actor's commit in the moved range lowered, which no report names), each to the count measured at the new pin, and the same pointer change set without any one of those lowerings gives 10 at S3 (T040, T042a); the producing task records that set before the pointer run, each row with its source (the run id of its report, or the commit of another actor that lowered it), measured with the S3 ratchet measurement of `scripts/repo/validate_cheap.sh` (T040) over those files (UNCONFIRMED until T040 lands that the helper runs check-only outside a CPA run; otherwise the set is read from a first pointer run's S3 refusal, which names every such row with nothing moved), and T441 and T580a check that the lowered set equals the set S3 computes; a key that is new or above its row in those files stays `baseline_drift` and is never lowered or raised by the pointer change set; a key that a layer fast-forward, a late catch-up, the constitution update or a CPA merge brings into a scored repository outside the declared files and that no `baseline_lowering_owed` report covers is reported `baseline_drift`, never a refusal of the run that meets it, and is registered through T092 at the next window, its owed action a fix of the file (a count that the drift lowered closes when a change set lowers the row to it, at the latest the pointer change set above).
- **CPA check stages** (T318, T394a, T503, T504a, T514, T535, T537, T538, T543, T564): every check that a P4-P7 task wires into CPA is a row of the check registry `scripts/repo/validate_checks.tsv` (T040; name, command, image, mode `plain`, `ratchet` or `deferred`, baseline file, and scope `files` or `changeset`), added in the change set that wires it and reviewed with it; that change set also adds the check's command file to `scripts/repo/cpa_code.txt` (the path-class table of T042: the command file of every registered check and the list itself are class G-GATE) and holds the command file, the list and the registry row on a G-GATE verdict (an unheld edit refused with 20, `path_gate_unheld`), the registry's `# review:` header naming that verdict, a verdict of the registering work package whose gate list includes G-GATE (it may hold the package's other gated paths too when its list holds their gates, contracts revision 16, T042); the new check stays `check_pending_release` until the owner approves its GO in `cpa-host` (T042 rev 32; Released helper bullet), so its real-stage control needle below runs only after that approval, as a follow-up step of its own (T318a for `oasdiff_breaking`), never inside the review that releases it; every later registration (T394a, T503, T504a, T514, T535, T537, T538, T543 and T564) has the same post-release step without a task id of its own (it is named in the exit checks: the P5 exit record of T457 for T394a, the P6 exit record of T557 for T503, T504a, T514, T535, T537, T538 and T543, and the WP-71 checkpoint of P7 for T564): a scratch change set that the stage must refuse is run through the real stage and must exit 10 naming the check, and a golden-good one must pass, both CPA run records captured with `evrec`. Every such real-stage step (T288b, T318a and these) runs under three rules (rev 34, round-33 review B1, I2, M6; rev 35, round-34 review I2, I3, I4, I6, m3, m4): (i) harness and trust state, as CENTRAL C3 defines it and not restated here (the P6-P7 bullet "CPA fixture harness and trust state" cites the same definition): each case runs on a fresh T039 harness clone with its own test-state `CPA_HOST_STATE` and a fresh throwaway bare remote, never a hosted URL or the working path, every submodule of the clone initialised from the local checkout's object store with its remote replaced by its own throwaway bare repository (CENTRAL C3(d)), every clone and remote of the step built from the same base, main HEAD at the start of the step; the test state starts from the adoption of CENTRAL C3(a) (the recorded T047 adoption, or before it the fixture adoption) and replays, in ascending numeric `<n>` order of `$EV/hc/owner-trust/<n>.json` (never lexical order), every recorded owner-trust record whose GO was introduced before the GO under test, reproducing each record's flags exactly (`--recovery`, the typed override answer through `script(1)`) and its retire, revoke and reanchor rows (CENTRAL C3(c)), and none whose GO was introduced after it (an approval skipped in that replay makes a later recorded approval of the replay give 20 `reviewed_files_incomplete`, the CENTRAL C3 fixture, never a blind result); the pending golden-bad case runs on that replayed state WITHOUT the GO under test (CENTRAL C3(b)), and the approved golden-bad and approved golden-good cases each run after one more scripted test-state approval, of the GO under test, with the commit and flags of its own owner-trust record (CENTRAL C3(c)); so a golden-bad commit that the pending case lets through, and the golden-good commit that S5 makes and S6 pushes, reach only their own case's bare repository and never the base of another case; (ii) precondition, checked before anything runs: the owner's real `cpa-host --show` manifest (agents run only read-only modes such as `--show` against the owner's state and never approve, retire, revoke or reanchor there, CENTRAL C3(e)) holds the check's command file with a sha256 equal to that file's entry in the `reviewed_files` of the newest owner-approved GO that lists the command file, which is the GO under test of the step (a later approved GO that changes the command file moves the step to that GO, never blocks it; for such a later GO, which is not the registering GO, the pending case is omitted, because the old approved check runs there and exits 10, and only the approved cases judge it; the pending case runs for the registering GO only, rev 36 patch 1), and an approval record `$EV/hc/owner-trust/<n>.json` names that GO (CENTRAL C7) (a check that runs in an image takes its digest from the `build/containers/images.lock.yaml` content that the replay reproduces, with no sha256 equality on that shared file); while any of them is missing the step is Operator-blocked, never run and never a reopen; (iii) outcomes: in the pending case (registering GO only, (ii)) the approved snapshot lacks the check's registry row and command file and the golden-bad change set, which declares no registry row, must exit 14 with `CHECK_PENDING_RELEASE` naming the check in `Deferred-Gates:` and without exit 10 (the check did not run; CENTRAL C1); in the approved golden-bad case it must exit 10 naming the check; in the approved golden-good case it must pass (no exit 10 or 20, and an exit 14 only for deferrals that do not name the check, each listed in the step's record); only a stage that, with (ii) met and the harness approval made, still exits 0 or 14 without naming the check in the approved golden-bad case is blind and reopens the registering task, while a run report naming `check_pending_release` for the check in an approved case means the replay or the approval did not take effect, and, per CENTRAL C3(f), an exit 20 that the case does not name as its expected refusal means a harness or trust-state defect (the run report names its refusal code), as does an exit 10 in the pending case from another approved check or an exit 10 in the approved golden-good case: each stops the step for a repair of the harness or its fixture, never a reopen and never read as the check being blind. Changed rows (CENTRAL C1; rev 33, round-32 review I3): `scripts/repo/validate_checks.tsv` and `scripts/qa/guard_registry.tsv` are keyed by their first column; a key absent from the approved copy runs only in the run whose change set declares its row, held on a G-GATE verdict (the registration case), and is otherwise `check_pending_release`, never run and never failing, while a HEAD-only `scripts/qa/guard_registry.tsv` key never changes a test's lane; for a key present in the approved copy the approved row governs, a differing HEAD or declared row for that key is reported `check_pending_release` with that row and does not take effect, and mode strictness never drops below the approved row; so a row change (the T394a `eslint` change from `deferred` to `ratchet`, a changed image or baseline column, the guard-polarity changes from `RED_EXPECTED` to GREEN that T383, T399 and T413 make on the T334a registry) takes effect only once the owner has approved its GO, and the post-release step of the first such change (the T394a `eslint` row) adds a harness case: a declared row that sets the approved `ratchet` row back to `deferred` does not weaken the stage (the approved row runs: the run report names the `eslint` refusal of the golden-bad file and `check_pending_release` with the declared row, and the exit is 10 by the T040 exit precedence of a refusal beside a pending check, nothing committed, never 0 and never 14); paired mutation: a union in which the declared row governs records no `eslint` refusal for that golden-bad file; and it is one of two kinds. A per-file check (scope `files`: it is given declared files and judges each of them; the `eslint` and `prettier` rows of T394a, `export_sync` of T535, the per-file documentation gates of T538, `squawk` of T543 and `protected_spec` of T564) takes the `files`/`types` scope of its check (plan owner's rule (Z)), and, unless its name is already in the closed check set of the check class row of the abbreviation table (as `eslint` and `prettier` are), its change set adds the check's row for every class to `scripts/repo/check_classes.tsv` (`yes` or `no`, each with its reason; T040b, plan owner's rule (V); next bullet) under the table-review form of the next bullet, with a golden-false fixture through the real stage (a file passes at a path of a class whose row says `no` and the same bytes give 10 at a `source` path; for a documentation gate, a `docs/register/Issues.md` of class `generated` whose quoted ticket text holds the word TODO passes) and its paired mutation in the T043 form (with that class row set to `yes`, the exempt file gives 10), so it never fires on a byte-exact evidence, generated or legacy-collection file; the class loader refuses with 20 (`check_unknown`, T040b) a check of scope `files` whose name has no class rows, never applying a default. A change-set check (scope `changeset`: it takes no declared-file list and judges the change set as a whole; `oasdiff_breaking` of T318, `coverage_gate` of T503, the mutation-score and observable-assertion stages of T504a, `perf_cheap` of T514, `badges` of T537, the link and scope gates of T538, and `schema_doc_diff` and `tbls_diff` of T543) is outside the class table, which its registry row states. Either kind is check-only: it reads the tracked tree and writes only under its run's `$CPA_RUN` (a generator or formatter runs in its check or diff form, or on a copy under the run's `/out`, never rewriting a tracked file; the binding design of T042); and its golden-bad fixture is also run once through the real CPA stage path, not only through the check's own test, as a control needle proving that the stage can see (§11.4.201(7)(c)). A check that judges a release candidate rather than a change set is a release-seam check (P6-P7 conventions), not a CPA stage.

1,024,000 B, a ledger-named blob unbounded and listed as an OD-76 owed relocation), `evidence-ledger` (the hash-chained `$EV/ledger.jsonl` and the append-only `$EV/flake_ledger.jsonl`, under the bound that T040b derives from the projected entry count, raised only by its held reviewed table change on a G-DATA review iteration), `patches`, `governance-carrier` (`.specify/memory/constitution-appendix.md` and `submodules/constitution/Constitution.md`, the private-key check skipping only the exact lines of `scripts/repo/private_key_carriers.tsv`, 4,194,304 B), `legacy-collection` (the kept legacy collections `docs/issues/**` and the S-12 root reports: no `revision_header` check) and `fixtures`; round-25 review M3); a path that rows of two classes match is refused with 20 (`class_ambiguous`); a table change counts only with its review: the table's header line `# review: <verdict path>` names the verdict, which holds GO in the main-repository HEAD, is declared with GO in the same change set, or holds the change as a held commit on exactly that verdict (plan owner's rule (X)), and otherwise S3 gives 10 (`class_table_unreviewed`) and the change set is judged with the tables of its HEAD; even a reviewed table change applies only to the paths held on its own verdict: every other path of the change set is judged with the HEAD tables, and a path whose result differs between the two table sets without being held on that verdict is refused with 20 (`table_admits_unheld_path`, T040b), so a task that adds a row declares every file the row admits held on the same verdict as the row. So every P4-P7 record or capture under `$EV/` and `$AUD/` with those suffixes (the contract reports of T314 to T321 under `$AUD/contract/`, the security, desktop and web reports under `$AUD/`, the qa outputs, `$EV/release_digests/`, `$EV/verify/final.json`, `$EV/pack/`) is class `evidence` with no row of its own (`$EV/flake_ledger.jsonl` is class `evidence-ledger`, T563), and the register dump, exports and reconciliation outputs are class `generated` (T574, T577). A P4-P7 task that commits other tracked files that a generator writes either writes them so that they pass every check of class `source` (for example a final newline, no trailing whitespace, a size under 1,024,000 B and, on Markdown, a revision header), which needs no row, or adds their `generated` row in its change set under the table review form above, its header naming that task's review verdict and the files the row admits declared held on that same verdict, with a golden-false fixture through the real S2 or S3 path (the same bytes at a path that no row names give 10 or 13) and its paired mutation in the T043 form (with the row dropped, the file the row admits gives 10): the rows this task list expects are T535 and T536 for the export twins and `docs/EXPORT_MANIFEST.json`, and, where their generators cannot meet the `source` checks, T523 (`docs/reference/collections/`), T537 (`docs/status/badges/`), T541 (`docs/reference/schema/`) and T546 (`docs/reference/api/routes.json`); a file above its class bound is never admitted by a raised bound without a held reviewed table change carrying the measured size (T040b). Evidence files that carry bare 40- or 64-hex strings (verdicts with `covers_runs`, findings, verifier JSON, run records, digests) pass the S2 secret fold only through the hex-hash filter of its baseline (`--exclude-secrets '^([0-9a-f]{40}|[0-9a-f]{64})$'`, recorded in the baseline's `filters_used`, T040a), never through an exemption: a fake secret assembled at run time in such a file still gives 13. A raw tool output above 1,024,000 B, or whose suffix is none of those of class `evidence` (an `.xml` or `.html` report, for example), is kept only as the ledger-named blob `$EV/blobs/<sha256>` of its `evrec` capture, never at a path of its own under `$EV/` or `$AUD/`, where it would exceed the class bound or be class `source`; one within the bound whose suffix is one of class `evidence` (a `.tsv` table, the Android lint SARIF of T426) may keep a path of its own, byte for byte. Every Markdown file that a P4-P7 task creates at a path whose class applies the `revision_header` check (T040b; an `$EV/**/*.md` file is class `source` too) carries the §11.4.44 revision header (S3 `revision_header`, T040), and a P4-P7 task that edits an existing Markdown file of a class that applies the check and that has no header adds it in the same change (the basis of the T092 `legacy headerless documents` item, T576) and removes that file's `(revision_header, <path>, missing)` row in the same change set, or, in a `--repo` run, has the row reported `baseline_lowering_owed` (inherited rule (c)). Class `legacy-collection` holds the kept collections that no task edits (T040b): a P4-P7 task that edits a file of that class drops the file's exact-path row in the same change set under the table review form above, the edited file held on that change's verdict because its class changes, and adds the §11.4.44 revision header that the file then needs as class `source` (T531 for `SECURITY_AUDIT_REPORT.md`, T524 for a root working doc that it merges or keeps live; no task edits a `docs/issues` ticket); an archived file that no task edits keeps the class at its new path (T524); (T040b states this rule). In P6 every change to the path-class table (T523, T524, T531, T535, T536, T537, T541, T546) is held on the one serial verdict `$EV/reviews/WP-63-path-classes[-r<n>].json`, reviewed by T539, whatever verdict the task names for its other files, because `scripts/repo/check_exemptions.tsv` carries a single `# review:` header; a table change starts only once the previous held table change's GO is committed in the main repository's HEAD, so no two table changes are held at once.

### Standing merge review, P4 to P7 (stream ST-REV)

The merges that CPA makes in a submodule are reviewed by the reviewer of the range they merge into (Diverged repository bullet); every merge that CPA makes in the main repository from the first P4 window to the closing push is reviewed by this one standing task, the P4-P7 counterpart of the merge-file reviews that the P0-P1 conventions give ST-REV for the P0 to P2 windows and that T307 makes for P3. It belongs to no work package of docs/21 §5 and has no checkpoint of its own: a merge it has not yet accepted keeps the range above it unpushed (S6, T042).

a merge made after the T566 candidate was built is also judged against that candidate: an incoming range that touches only test paths (the patterns of `scripts/release/test_path_patterns.tsv`, written with T566; the test-only acceptance is refused until the T566a GO `$EV/reviews/WP-71-test-paths.json` is in the main repository's HEAD, a merge then needing the rebuild proof or a candidate re-cut; re-checked by T580a (c)) is accepted on the T567 and T568 records; verdict GO in that merge-review file with every required `review-verdict/1` field, its gate list including `G-GATE` when the merge brought a foreign change to a G-GATE path (foreign CPA code, which S1 integrates only by a held merge) or resolved a conflict in such a file (T040, T042; contracts revision 16), in which case `reviewed_files` lists every G-GATE path the merge changed with its sha256 (CENTRAL C6), and `covers_runs` naming the merge run (repository path, commit sha, `CPA-Run` id), committed in the main repository's HEAD by the next window or by the re-run's own declared change set (T039), after which S6 pushes the range as soon as the held commits below the merge are released by their own verdicts; ## Phase P5: Remediation (docs/21 §3.3 P5, §5.6)

**Entry**: P4 accepted for the contracts each fix touches; each register item root-caused (FR-008).
**Ordering**: server first, then each client against the fixed contract; within a stream by severity then exposure (docs/15 §13; the ODG-35 working default, no SLA tiers); a contract-changing fix lands with its client changes and both-sided tests in one reviewed change set. Every [TDD] fix task of P5 follows the Fix protocol (FP) bullet of the P4-P5 conventions above (FP covers only [TDD] fix tasks; a [REVIEW] task, a record-only task such as T355, T357 or T447 and a push or pointer task such as T433, T440c or T442 follows its own text, and the `CPA --repo <path>` users are exactly those the FP bullet lists).

**Owner-blocked legs (P5 edges)**: an owner-blocked leg is a part of a task marked BLOCKED-ON an ODG or OD id with no research.md default (today: T348 encryption and key management ODG-27 with the SQLite production keying OD-68; T355 TLS ODG-26 and the BC-19 leg of T376 that goes with it; the BC-22 removal leg of T376 ODG-23; the `submodules/llms_verifier` handling of T438 ODG-14; the desktop signing rows of T450 ODG-06; and any other leg so marked). A depends-on edge of P5 onto a task that has owner-blocked legs is satisfied once (a) every unblocked leg of that task is done (its RED and GREEN records, its review verdict GO and its change set pushed) and (b) each blocked leg is recorded on its register item (`docs/workable_items.db`) as Operator-blocked (§11.4.21) with its ODG or OD id and exact reason, plus an `ev/1` entry through `tools/evidence/evrec` citing that item; never `Fixed`, and never `blocked-unavailable` (that term is reserved for an absent service, credential, device or host). The dependent task proceeds, and T457 carries every such leg into `$EV/p5-exit.json` as a blocked item. A [REVIEW] task is never itself marked BLOCKED-ON: when a change set it reviews belongs to an owner-blocked leg, that change set cannot exist yet, so the edge onto the [REVIEW] task is satisfied once every unblocked leg it reviews holds GO (its verdict committed) and each blocked leg is recorded per (b); the blocked leg is reviewed later as that task's continuation, as below. The blocked legs per [REVIEW] task are derived when T457 runs from the BLOCKED-ON markers of the tasks it reviews, never from this list; at rev 26 they include T359 for T339, T341, T348, T349, T354, T355 and T358; T379 for T362 (ODG-20), T374 and T376; T395 for T383 (ODG-24), T385, T386 and T387; T411 for T401, T402, T407, T409 (ODG-23 and ODG-24) and T410; T428 for T412 (ODG-29, its one blocked case), T416, T417, T419, T421, T422 and T424 (T423 carries no owner-blocked leg, its device row being `blocked-unavailable`). T457 refuses a [REVIEW] edge whose verdict set omits an unblocked leg with `review_leg_missing`, and one counting a blocked leg as reviewed with `blocked_leg_reviewed` (fixtures and mutation in T457). A task whose only input is the blocked leg's own output is itself blocked with the same id and recorded the same way, never awaited by its dependents (T360 for the S-05 migration of T348). When a leg is unblocked later, no satisfied edge is reopened: the leg runs as its own tracked continuation of its task, reviewed by that task's review, and its review joins T457's inputs only if its GO is committed before the P5 cut point of T455, otherwise it is carried to P6 on its register item.
**Exit**: every finding in each stream `Fixed` with custody chain or closed by an allowed basis; blocked items listed with exact reason.
