## Phase P6: Test closure, QA, performance, documentation (WP-60 to WP-65)

**Purpose**: close every applicable test-type cell, convert the HelixQA banks into asserting cases, install the performance gate, and deliver the documentation and definitions programme (docs/21 §3.3 P6).

**Entry**: WP-24 QA wrapper and validator, WP-23 applicability map and baselines, WP-38 performance baselines, WP-37 documentation baseline, WP-40 live route dump, WP-41 contract tests.

**Phase-group conventions (P6-P7)** (all paths repo-relative):

- `$SPEC` = `$FEAT` = `specs/001-full-project-audit-remediation`; `$EV` = `$SPEC/evidence` (doc06 §11 layout: `ledger.jsonl` with `ev/1` entries, `verdicts/<item-id>.json` derived only, `anchors.jsonl`, `matrix/`, `reviews/` for every `[REVIEW]` verdict, `hc/` for human-checkpoint records); `$AUD` = `$SPEC/audit`. The doc06 §11 per-application coverage folders are `$EV/coverage_baseline/<app>/` (the P2 baselines and exclusion-gate records of WP-23, read here as the ratchet floor) and `$EV/coverage_targets/<app>/` (the dated owner targets, ODG-17), both named this way because `.gitignore:139` ignores every directory named `coverage/` at any depth and no WP-09 negation covers it below the root (docs/21 IC-38). `(new)` and `.gitignore` rules as in the P4-P5 conventions.
- `TIC` = the containerized runner `scripts/test-in-container.sh <app> <lane> -- <cmd>` (created in WP-12 (T121) over the T120 wrappers; lanes `unit`, `contract`, `integration`, `e2e`, `api`, `docs`, `tooling` and `rust` (the `rust` lane and the app keys `catalogizer-api-client`, `catalogizer-desktop`, `installer-wizard`, `build-scripts` and one per TypeScript submodule added by T200a, on which every TIC call with them depends); doc05 §12.5). The rows of the `qa` app (`TIC qa <lane>`) dispatch to `scripts/containers/run_qa.sh` in IMG-QA, the WP-24 QA image of T211 (helixqa, Tesseract, ffmpeg, Playwright browsers); `run_qa.sh` and those rows are delivered by T212, on which every `TIC qa` call below depends (each such task names it together with T211). No test or build runs on the bare host (§11.4.173); every build of a deliverable artifact and every compile-class lane (mutation runs in IMG-MUT included) is submitted to the remote build host through `scripts/build/dispatch.sh` (T005b; driver `cmd/distributed-build`, manifest checked by `scripts/build/verify_artifact.sh`) and resumed by its registered callback, its RED and GREEN evidence taken from the callback records (T121a contract), no compile-class lane running locally (T121b); the remote-group, input-closure, resumed-S1, split-lane and image-class rules (a) to (e) of the P4-P5 block apply; when no qualified build host is reachable, or the dispatch fails for another closed reason, it is `blocked-unavailable` with that reason (the closed T005b reasons: `host_unreachable`, `no_qualified_host`, `build_liveness_lost`, `build_progress_flat`, `build_wallclock_exceeded`, `driver_secret_lost`, `artifact_unavailable`, and `signing_key_not_provisioned` for a provenance-signing step; apart from these, and never `blocked-unavailable`: `snapshot_mismatch` is detected on the build host and recorded `infra_failed` (T005b), `submodule_uninitialised` and `undeclared_dirty_input` are caller defects that CPA refuses with exit 20, as are `closure_incomplete` (an input closure missing a file the build reads) and `remote_moved_while_suspended` (a remote that moved while a run was suspended), and a CPA remote S3 check that cannot run is `remote_check_unavailable`, exit 20, distinct from a failing check, exit 10), never a local or bare-host build, hosts read only through `build/hosts.env` (T137a, T137), a lane needing the WP-13 stack being a T121a split lane (remote compile, local run of the digest-verified binaries), and only the host identity stays the owner input ODG-07; docs run in IMG-DOCS, QA in IMG-QA.
- `CPA` = `scripts/commit-push-all.sh` (WP-04, IC-16), invoked through the owner-installed host entry point `cpa-host` (T042, rev 32; `cpa-host <args>` passes every CPA argument, `--run-id`, `--resume` and `--repo` included, to the owner-approved CPA, so `CPA <args>` here means `cpa-host <args>`): every commit and push of this task list goes through it, on `main` only, fast-forward only, never `--force` (§11.4.113, FR-020, FR-024); work inside a submodule repository uses its per-repository mode `CPA --repo <path>`, which moves no ancestor HEAD or gitlink and records its pending pin move in `.audit/pending_pins.tsv` (FP step 7 of the P4-P5 block); a run ending with exit code 16 `awaiting_remote_checks` has committed nothing and is resumed, never counted as committed (P4-P5 commit-window bullet); CPA writes nothing into the tracked tree, its outputs stay in the ignored `.audit/commit-push/<run_id>/`, and a task cites a run report through `evrec` (the P4-P5 commit-push outputs rule).
- **CPA fixture harness and trust state** (CENTRAL C3; the one definition of the harness for P4 to P7: the P4-P5 CPA check-stage bullet cites it for its real-stage steps, and the P4 and P5 tasks follow it): every fixture of P4 to P7 that runs through the real CPA path (S0, S2, S3, S5 or S6; the phrases "through the real CPA path", "a scratch change set", "scratch clone" and "scratch trees" in a fixture below all mean this harness, except "the producing stream's scratch clone" (a fix stream's own clone outside this repository, T580e, which a fixture stands in for with a separate throwaway directory) and the T580c scratch clone (a named candidate clone)) runs on the T039 harness: a throwaway clone under the test's temporary directory with its own `CPA_HOST_STATE` and `CPA_HOST_ENTRY` there, its only remote a throwaway bare repository created under the same temporary directory and seeded from main HEAD (never a hosted URL and never the working path, so no fixture publishes anything; a fixture that needs two remotes creates two such bare repositories), and every owner approval it needs scripted through `script(1)` against that test state, its trust state built as CENTRAL C3 (revised, round 35) defines it (adopted at the recorded adoption of `$EV/wp04/adoption.json` once it exists, and before that at the C3(a) fixture adoption, a fixture G-GATE GO whose `reviewed_files` lists every CPA-executed file at the clone's HEAD, approved in the test state; then every recorded owner approval of `$EV/hc/owner-trust/*.json` introduced before the GO under test script-approved in order, each with `--commit <the exact sha its record names>` (never a recomputed I(v), C3(c)) and with the exact flags of its record (`--recovery` and the typed override answer replayed through `script(1)`), a working-tree record (the CENTRAL C11 recovery, naming no `--commit` sha) replayed with the clone checked out at the commit R its record names, the first holding its verdict and listed content, and then returned to the base commit (C3(c)), and every retire, revoke and reanchor row replayed in ascending numeric `<n>` order, never lexical (C3(c)); then, for an approved case only, the GO under test: a pending case uses that replayed state WITHOUT the GO under test, C3(b)); submodules of a harness clone are initialised from the local checkouts' object stores and every submodule remote is replaced by its own throwaway bare repository (C3(d)); agents may run the read-only `cpa-host --show` modes against the owner's state and never `approve`, `retire`, `revoke` or `reanchor` against it, and an image-digest check compares the manifest sha256 of `images.lock.yaml` with the blob of a named commit and then reads the digest from that blob (C3(e)); each case of a fixture on a fresh harness clone with a fresh bare remote built from the same base and trust state; agents never touch the owner's real `$CPA_HOST_STATE` or `$CPA_HOST_ENTRY` (the conductor rule is scoped to those; an agent may drive a test-state `cpa-host`); because the approved copy's rows stay in force under the union rule (CENTRAL C1), a paired mutation that removes a row from a CPA table or path list (`scripts/release/release_seam_files.txt`, `scripts/repo/path_gates.tsv`, `scripts/repo/cpa_code.txt`, `scripts/repo/validate_checks.tsv`, `scripts/qa/guard_registry.tsv`) commits the list without the row in the scratch history and approves that version in the scratch state, and is caught when the change set that the fixture holds unheld is then accepted; removing a row from a working-tree copy alone is never the mutation; the path-class table and the other T040b tables (`scripts/repo/check_exemptions.tsv`, `scripts/repo/check_classes.tsv`, `scripts/repo/private_key_carriers.tsv`, `scripts/repo/validate_baselines/**`) are not union tables: they are read under the HEAD held-table rule of T040b, so a mutation removing one of their rows is a held HEAD change set under that rule, never an approval; every CPA git call in these fixtures, and every git call of a helper run through `cpa-host --exec-approved`, carries `-c core.hooksPath=<empty no-hooks directory>` (CENTRAL C4: the run's own directory for a CPA run, a directory inside the fresh exec directory for `--exec-approved`); an exit 20 in a case of such a fixture that the case does NOT name as its expected refusal (the run report names its refusal code, compared with the code the case expects) means a harness or trust-state defect, repaired before the fixture is read, never a reopen of the task under test; an exit 20 whose code IS the case's named expected refusal (for example `verdict_already_go`, `path_gate_unheld`, `hook_outputs_gated`, `accepted_pins_*`, `release_seam_unreleased`, `holder_pid_not_ancestor` or `run_id_invalid`, or an S0 undeclared-file refusal that the case expects naming that file, as in T580e (ii) and (iii)) is that case's result, compared code and named path alike; likewise an exit 10 in a pending case that comes from another approved check (not the check under test), or any exit 10 in an approved golden-good case, stops the step for fixture repair (CENTRAL C3(f), round 35; rule (iii) of the P4-P5 CPA check-stage bullet).
- Review before push, generated tracked files, commit windows and register writes: the P4-P5 rules apply unchanged (a change made before the `[REVIEW]` GO that covers it is committed as a held commit, `Awaits-Review: <verdict file>`, and pushed only once that verdict file is committed in the main repository's HEAD with GO and lists the held commit's `CPA-Run` id in `covers_runs`, the path always resolved against the main repository whichever repository holds the commit, enforced at S6; a hold on a verdict file already GO is refused with 20, `verdict_already_go`; a repository whose remote moved while it holds unpushed commits is integrated only by the CPA merge of the diverged-repository rule, held on its own merge-review file `$EV/reviews/CPA-merge-<run_id>.json` and reviewed by the reviewer that bullet names (the standing merge review T308a for the main repository), never by a merge made by hand; a container writes generated tracked files under `/out` and a host step copies them with matching sha256; uncommitted work of parallel streams is committed in the P0-P1 commit windows by the conductor (ST-GOV), and no stream declares another stream's files; every mutating `$WI` or `sqlite3` command on `docs/workable_items.db` runs through `scripts/register/locked.sh` (T064) in IMG-TESTUTIL, bulk writes with the SQLite `.backup` pre-op backup through `scripts/register/backup_db.sh` (T064a; never `cp -al`) and the T066 dump-and-commit procedure; CPA check stages registered in `scripts/repo/validate_checks.tsv` with their scope and, for a per-file check, its class rows, check-only and needle-proven through the real stage path; the inherited disk-headroom, `docs/scripts/README.md` row and ratchet-baseline rules and the path-class rules of the P4-P5 block apply too).
- "Three-run evidence" = three runs with identical canonical hashes recorded in `$EV/ledger.jsonl` (doc06 §5, SC-003). "Paired mutation" = a mutation observed to turn the test RED, recorded with `mutation: {operator, location, result: "caught"}` (doc05 §8.2).
- `[REVIEW]` tasks are pure reviews owned by stream ST-REV on Opus at xhigh (§11.4.209), started through the Workflow `agent()` path (the dispatch path that sets model and effort) and carrying the review provenance record that T094a and T094d check, never by the producing stream (§11.4.240), iterate to zero blocking findings (§11.4.134), record at least one reviewer-authored mutation where a test or gate is reviewed (§11.4.194(6)(d)), and write their verdict to `$EV/reviews/<WP>[-<item>][-r<n>].json` (a merge commit that CPA makes being held on its own `$EV/reviews/CPA-merge-<run_id>.json`, P4-P5 Diverged repository bullet) in the `review-verdict/1` format of the P4-P5 block (`schema`, `verdict`, `blocking_findings`, `covers_runs`, `model` and `effort`, every field the schema requires); any fix goes back to the producing stream.
- **Gate-class holds**: a review verdict's `gate` field is a string or a list (contracts revision 16), so one verdict can hold paths of several path classes when its gate list carries each gate those paths require; every change set of P6-P7 that adds or edits a row of `scripts/repo/validate_checks.tsv` or a check command file that such a row names (both G-GATE paths in `path_gates.tsv`), an `images.lock.yaml` entry or a `cpa_code.txt` file holds those paths on a named verdict whose gate list includes G-GATE (a separate `-gate` verdict file is not required for it), and each commit carries exactly one `Awaits-Review:`; the tables `scripts/repo/check_exemptions.tsv`, `scripts/repo/check_classes.tsv`, `scripts/repo/private_key_carriers.tsv` and `scripts/repo/validate_baselines/**` are outside `cpa_code.txt`: they are governed by the T040b table-review form (their `# review:` header naming the verdict that holds them), never by a G-GATE hold of their own, so a task of this phase group that edits them (T472, T474, T580b (4), the T581 root run) holds them under T040b and never needs a G-GATE verdict for them.
- **Release seam**: CPA has no release mode (T042). A check that this task list calls a release-seam check (the performance verdict of T514, the escape-ratchet and catchability gates of T554 in their two named modes, `scripts/qa/escape_gates.sh --seam pre-qa --candidate <T566 fingerprint>` (at T569: no manual-QA cycle of the candidate is required; it runs at two named points: T569 (every release-seam check on the final candidate fingerprint, the performance verdict included, the escape gates in `--seam pre-qa --candidate <fingerprint>` mode) and T582 (every release-seam check re-run, the escape gates in `--seam final --candidate <fingerprint>` mode, on that fingerprint before the final verification is accepted, its output written under `.audit/out/<op_id>/` and cited in T582's `ev/1` entry); a refusal at any of them blocks the candidate exactly as a FAIL does (§11.4.135), and an absent verdict is a refusal, never a pass. Release-seam scripts are held by CPA, not by prose (rev 25; data-file scope rev 26): every release-seam script, and every data file it reads to reach its verdict, is listed by tracked path in `scripts/release/release_seam_files.txt` (new, one path per line, created by T042 with the `release_seam` path class), which the `release_seam` row of `scripts/repo/path_gates.tsv` (T042) maps to G-GATE, so a change to a listed file or to the list itself is a gate-class change that CPA holds on a named verdict whose gate list includes G-GATE (else 20, `path_gate_unheld`, T042); ## Dependencies and execution order

- Phase order is strict at the exit gates: **P0 -> P1 -> P2 -> P3 -> P4 -> P5 -> P6 -> P7**. The gate evidence for each phase is the `Checkpoint` line of its last work package plus the human checkpoints HC-1..HC-n in docs/21 section 3.3.
- Inside a phase, work packages follow the Inputs column of docs/21 section 5 (diagram in docs/21 section 5.9, which documents its two-way part edges between paired packages; the task-level dependency graph below is acyclic, checked by script). Tasks marked `[P]` inside one work package, and work packages with disjoint Inputs, may run concurrently, bounded by the host limits in docs/21 section 4.2 (60 percent memory ceiling, process-limit headroom, at most 6 concurrent agents).
- Producer and reviewer streams are separate: `[REVIEW]` tasks belong to ST-REV and never to the stream that produced the work (WP-39R, WP-74R).
- **Counts (rev 36: no id added or removed in any slice; recounted by script over the merged rev 36 file, two independent parsers agreeing, every figure unchanged from rev 35, rev 34, rev 33 and rev 32)**: 676 tasks, the 595 frozen ids T001-T595 plus 81 suffix ids (rev 14 added T435c, T440b and T447b, rev 15 added T440c in P5 and T137a in WP-09, rev 17 added T442a and T442b in P5 and T580c in P7, rev 18 added T566a in P7, rev 19 added T084a and T175a in the head half and T580d in P7, rev 22 added T420a in P5 and T139a in the head half, rev 23 adds T200a in P2, T225a, T225b, T240a, T241a, T254a, T272a, T277a, T277b, T288a and T288b in P3, T318a, T322a, T334a and T336a in P4, T456a, T456b and T456c (new WP-58) in P5 and T580e in P7, and tags T449, T499 and T502 `[TDD]`, rev 24 adds T225c and T254b in P3 and T564a and T580f in P7, and tags T106 `[TDD]`, rev 25 adds T134a in P1, rev 26 adds T225d and T225e in P3, rev 27 and rev 28 add none, rev 29 adds T335a (`[TDD]`) in P4 and T570a (`[REVIEW]`) in P7, rev 30 and rev 31 add none, rev 32 adds T046a (`[REVIEW]`, the owner install checkpoint) in P0 and none elsewhere, rev 33, rev 34, rev 35 and rev 36 add none); 318 tagged `[TDD]`, 86 tagged `[REVIEW]`, 115 tagged `[P]`, 80 tagged `[SUBAGENT]`, every task tagged `[USn]`; P4 to P7 hold 326 of them (178 `[TDD]`, 48 `[REVIEW]`); rev 33 adds no id (the released-seam precheck `scripts/release/seam_released.sh` landed inside T564a; rev 34 drops it, CENTRAL C8, still with no id change), every figure above recounted by script over the merged rev 36 file, two independent parsers agreeing. ## Implementation strategy

1. **MVP / first deliverable**: P0 and P1 (verifier, evidence recorder, register, pinned containers), then P2 baselines. After P2 exit the register contains every known item and the baselines exist, which already satisfies US1 on its own.
2. **Incremental delivery**: each later phase ends at a checkpoint that is independently demonstrable (audit accepted at G-AUDIT, contract layer, remediation per component, test closure, final verification).
3. **Parallel team strategy**: streams ST-INFRA, ST-QA, ST-GOV, ST-REG, ST-SEC, ST-API, ST-WEB, ST-DESK, ST-AND, ST-SUB, ST-DOC, ST-PERF and ST-REV work in parallel once their phase gate opens.

- Paths, scripts and tool facts proposed by the plan and not yet verified are labelled `(new)` or UNCONFIRMED in the task text; nothing in this list has been executed.
